Two days in the wine region of Casablanca and Leyda Valley were well enjoyed, followed by some stunning biking in the Andes, capped off with a hike on our final day of the tour. The staff all made us feel so welcome in Chile, and were informative the entire trip. Lunches were absolutely delicious, with home cooked meals brought along each day, and we enjoyed picnics at some beautiful points overlooking valleys, and mountains. We really appreciated that Andres and Ines were able to customize the tour to accommodate our entire group, as we were traveling with young children, and everything turned out really well. Everyone in our group raved about the trip and we toasted with some tasty Chilean wine on our last evening, to a successful biking trip. I highly recommend booking a tour with them- we hope to be back again one day!

review_text: I have booked my trip with WWT in Uyuni, Bolivia and have spent 3 days and 2 nights in this incredible place that everyone should experience at least once in their lifetime. I have read so many horror stories about cars breaking down, poor driving skills, bad food, so talked to a few agencies prior commiting to do this trip with WWT. And it was the best decision ever - our driver was very skilled, very knowledgable, amazing cook, and when it comes to personality, the nicest person ever. I was the only vegetarian on board, yet he ensured I always had something to eat, and saying that, we never went hungry, even enjoyed a bottle of wine on our first night. Me and my fellow travellers wanted the tour to end in San Pedro de Atacama, and at the time of our visit the nearest border was closed. And this is where our guide stood out - he was checking on the situation daily, keeping us informed and always giving us options to choose from (what do we want to see, do, etc.). One of my fellow travellers developed symptoms of altitude sickness. He was extremely caring, patient and dealt with the situation with all due responsibility. On our last night he drove for 30 mins. so he could make a phone call with the office and check on the border situation. The following morning, he would make a 60km deroute and took us to the next available border crossing in Ollague where he organised for a bus connection to San Pedro. Last, but not least, he should be awarded special thanks for his photography skills :-) So thank you, WWT, I not only had the best time ever, but also made friends for life!

review_text: While in Chile for an adventure conference I booked a climb of Osorno Volcano. After being collected from the airport and transferred to the hut for an overnight with dinner (very good food) to allow for an early start we enjoyed an outdoor hot tub with fantastic views and a pair of Condors circling above. The trip from the airport was in itself an interesting little tour with a couple of stops to see some interesting spots on the way with an instantly engaging Sandra as our guide. At the hut we met Jóse who briefed us on the plan for the following day and gave us some background to the area and Chile in general. After dinner we got our technical equipment and headed to bed. An early start, 5 AM brought us out into the cold darkness of predawn and we began to climb, alternating between sections of ash and snowfields. The previous 29 hours of flying was making its mark but as the dawn begun the rewards for being there made he effort worth it. By full light we had made good progress, the pace was reasonable and the terrain was now all snow. After a short stop for a snack at a ski station we carried on and shortly afterwards donned our harness, helmet and crampons to continue on harder snow and at a steeper gradient. At this point the lack of sleep and the effects of the long journey kicked in and it was time for a "mountaineering decision" to be made. We had reached about 2100M with a steep ridge remaining to the summit, the winds were very strong. So, would we go on? No, the decision was that the best course of action was a tactical withdrawal, the point was to enjoy the day not summit at any cost so we instead we roped up and traversed the glacier to the seracs where we had lunch while watching some climbers doing an ice route. The scenery was spectacular and the conditions fantastic. Jose is a great guide, technically excellent and with an easy personality and a great general knowledge of the area which he shares in an easy and friendly manner. I would recommend this day on the mountain to anyone, it is a strenuous climb but not beyond most reasonably fit people. Jose has the skills to provide the safety and provides good guidance for people on unfamiliar ground. All in all a great experience and I would hope to have another chance to make it to the summit. Thanks Jose and Sandra great job all round. Christy Sinclair

review_text: Where do I begin?... We booked 4 tours to see the vineyard Concha y Toro with Turistik at Parque Arauco. Gabriel at the Turistik booth made our reservation. He explained tours are in English, Spanish and Portuguese. We selected the 9:30 am tour. He asked for all of our names, which we gave him: 4 in total. Then when he handed the receipt we noticed he overcharged us: he booked 6 tours in total. We noticed when we saw the odd charge in the receipt and let him know. He had to issue a refund, which took him like 20 minutes in the phone, and we haven't received yet. Fine, anyone can make 1 mistake and banks take a while. Then we asked if the tour can pick us up at our hotel. We told him our hotel is nearby so he suggests we meet them "here" (at the booth) on Friday 9am to avoid being picked up too early. That's ok we say. The day of the tour we get into traffic and call at 8:55 to let them know we might be 5 minutes late. Valentina on the phone says she will let them know. We get to the Turistik booth and no one is there. After a while we ask the security person from Parque Arauco and he indicates the bus leaves from a different place (no one told us that when we made the reservation). We rush to to the parking lot where the buses leave, and I call Valentina again. She says we should rush and she will contact them again. We get there and the bus is obviously gone. After the bus is gone and we are furious, they tell us that the tour we were supposed to be in, it's only in Spanish and Portuguese. Even though we confirmed it was in English, we even made the reservation with Gabriel in English. (Gabriel claims he lived in the U.K., so he understands English). After rushing and calling and complaining (yes, very angry). Francisco, head of sales, says first, the bus is gone and there is nothing to do. Second, that we were late and called after 9 (tour leaves at 9), which infuriates me because I have the log on my phone saying I called at 8:55 am (and we were 5 minutes away), so I don't like being called a liar. Plus we waited for a while at the reservation booth where Gabriel told us to wait and no one was there. Third, they told us that the 9 am tour is only in Spanish and Portuguese. So, even if we managed to catch up, we would have ended up in a Spanish speaking tour (we were traveling with 3 English speakers). To top it all, when we ask for our refund, they tell us the reservation was made for 2 people (instead of 4), so they had to do a bunch of calls and system fixes to refund us back what we paid for. Now, I have 6 refunded ticket receipts, waiting for the money, which I have no idea if we will receive back at all, and a ruined last day of a trip to Chile. As a Chilean I feel absolutely embarrassed by everything that happened, and incredibly sad the people visiting from the U.K. with me have to leave with this awful experience and image of my country just because of the lack of professionalism of a "tourist" company. Added the image of the call log. First call before 9am. The rest were to complain. We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.

review_text: I spent 3.5 years/77 countries/150,000 miles traveling on my own motorcycle. Times have changed though and now, due to time constraints and moto-shipping costs, my "far away moto trips" are usually done on rentals. My wife and I rented from Daniel and Paula in March 2023 and were blown away by the professionalism and courtesy we were given. Let's be clear: There is nothing easy or cheap about running a motorcycle touring / rental company in a foreign country that has wildly high import taxes. Daniel has taken what has historically been a complex process and has made it incredibly easy to simply show up and ride. Registration/customs /immigration paperwork is handled in-house so that you can go back and forth between Argentina and Chile with no hassle. Since we rented two bikes and headed out on our own meanderings, I can't speak for the group tours. But I can speak for the quality of motorcycles we received and the guidance we were given prior to our road trip. I would highly recommend booking a rental or a tour with Moto Patagonia. The beauty of the region will make your jaw drop. Thank you to Daniel and Paula for providing an experience that's impossible to forget

review_text: I was under the impression that this Emporio was situated on Merced, and will review the restaurant at that location. We found this branch of Emporio after their other location sadly burnt down. As we had always enjoyed eating at the tables out in the garden there, we were delighted to find that this new( to us) location that is more downtown, has an even more extensive garden with lots of tables and ample shade from the sun for comfortable eating. As the name suggests, they seem to specialize in BBQ'd or grilled meats. Everything that we have tried so far has been perfectly cooked and very nicely presented. And unusually for Chile, not too highly salted!!! The wine selection is somewhat limited, I would like to see more from our local winery, San Pedro, on offer. We recognize some of the staff from the other restaurant, and received a great welcome when we " discovered" this new locale. The food and the service are both good and we hope that the restaurant is a great success.

review_text: On our first afternoon in Santiago, my husband and I visited this museum to learn more about this sober, but important time in Chile's history. The museum is very easy to get to as it is right across the street from the Quinta Normal metro station on the green line. Entry to the museum is free, but if you are not a Spanish speaker, we'd highly recommend getting the audio tour for CLP 2,000 per person. Almost all the signs are exclusively in Spanish, so you won't get much out of the museum unless you have the guide. The combination of the factual elements presented in the museum with the artistic presentation made for a really nice experience. We learned a lot about events leading up to Pinochet's dictatorship, the time during his reign, and events that led to his coming out of power. The museum contains many artifacts along with video footage and personal testimonies of people. We spent just shy of two hours here and would recommend a stop during your time in Santiago.

review_text: We stayed close to Puerto Natales and asked our hotel to organise the tour. I couldn't have been happier with the tour company they used. Patagonia Planet (sometimes called Planet Patagonia) was extremely professional, punctual and friendly. The company picked us up from our hotel and then we drove two hours to the park. It is a full day tour, we returned by 8.30pm. The group was small (8 people) and they organised us with one guide at the front and one at the rear of the group, thus everyone could walk at their own pace. The guides were in constant communication via walkie talkie's. A shortish walk up hill and then through a forest and then a more challenging ascent over boulders took my small group of three, four hours (we certainly set no record that day). The trek was hard, I'm fit (exercise five times a week, 48years old) and I found it challenging. In saying that I did set the pace and arrived at the top thirty minutes before some of our group who were less fit. They managed it so perhaps being fit is not a prerequisite. Some of our group had to turn back, but seemed to have an enjoyable wait in a lodge near the start. Either way, good boots, warm weather gear is a must, as is water. A packed lunch was provided as well as walking sticks. I wasn't sure if I needed a stick, but I'm glad I took up the offer of one. The view of the Torres deal Paine and glacial lake at the peak was well worth the climb. The guides had good english, and full of interesting information about the park. We toured in September and had an enjoyable day with not too many people, I'm not sure if I'ld like to do it in the peak season if there are masses of trekkers. Climbing to view Torres deal Paine was the highlight of our visit and Patagonia Planet made the journey stress free and enjoyable. Thanks for your comment Freoroamers! See you on your next adventure in Patagonia. It has been a pleasure to be part of your trip.

review_text: This should be a must do if you go to San Pedro de Atacama. We went with Cosmo Andino and they are really the best tour company in town! We were treated was a nice warm breakfast outside out bus before the trip. We had hot chocolate, coffee or tea and hot eggs and avocado with toast. It was actually quite amazing what they made for us in the space they had. Then when the sun started to rise we went off to see the geysers. review_text: Juan met us off the cruise ship and ensured we saw as much as possible in our 6 hours ashore. We saw all the important things, like the volcanoes, the debris left after the last eruption, the ski resort, the massive lake 880,000 square kilometres from so many different viewpoints and the main towns especially The City of Roses. He also took us off the beaten tracks to see Jersey cows being reared for milk, cheese and cream etc. Herefords being reared for meat and also Llamas. He pointed out wildlife including condors, and we remarked on the number of plants that grow well in England but are wild in Chile. (they obviously were brought back by the early discoverers.) He was witty, informative and a great driver stopping at brilliant places for photo opportunities. He even stopped when we saw a baby fox so we could take photos.He also stopped at places for us to get free wifi as he realised we needed opportunities to contact home. His car was superb, comfortable, with plenty of room for us to all see out and he could stop at small car parks and give us more understanding of the local area.. We went to extra different places than the big coach tours and it meant we had longer there than a big party would have had. Excellent tour and excellent value for money.

The tour includes the option of taking a lift up the first 400 m of height (has to be paid extra for). We had about 10 people in the group (all much younger than me in my 50s) with five guides. As a love climbing up I opted for the hike up, which most of the members of the group didn't. The guides strongly discouraged me in order to "save my power for the rest of the tour". I do a lot of hiking in the mountains of Japan alone, very often multiday treks with a heavy backpack) on mountain pathes rated medium to difficult, so I do know my limits and have no problems coping with 1400 m of height up and down in one day. Of course some people in the group where faster, so there was a faster and a slower group I joined). Unfortunately this resulted in the guide always telling us to hurry up, even prohibiting me sometimes to take pictures, always telling us "the group were waiting". We had 5 minutes on the volcano in the end ( as all agencies have the same timing there were hundreds of people up there within the same 30 minutes) and after climbing for 5 hours (the normal time) not even time for a real lunch break (just a couple of minutes to wolf down a sandwich) and to take in the absolutely beautiful views. The tour is being promoted as En esta excursión apreciarás las mejores vistas de la región ... To get down a long slide through the snow was scheduled. I would have much preferred to walk down, but there was no no time to do that. I was scared to slide down the steep mountain (no slide, you just put on waterproofs on sit down), so one of the guides told me that he would teach me and that I should trust him. He waited for me twice a bit further down and I tried to figure out how to control the speed. The third time he just snapped my foot and dragged me down the whole first part, completely ignoring me screaming. I was completely under shock when we finally came to a stop, couldn't breath, my whole body shaking, my heart racing, almost fainting and I couldn't get up at all. He just said he had to do that because I was to slow and there were other people coming and I should get up and continue. I told him that I couldn't and tried to explain the condition I was in. He showed no understanding at all and instead told me he would call the police and tell them that I was CAUSING trouble and I would be in trouble because of that (well, of cause ridiculous, just showing that he didn't know how to handle the situation). One of the other guides then took me down the other half of sliding, which with a bit of experience was no problem, but after the first experience definitely no fun. I arrived at the bottom 8,5 h after leaving (the tour was scheduled to last last between 8 and 9 hours), still shaking and with problems breathing, all related to the shock). When I tried to explain it to the lady at the office back in town, she just laughed at me. If you are young, fit, just interested in getting up and down as quickly as possible, than the tour might be right for you, Otherwise I hope you can find other options. Rosi

review_text: This is a memorial to those affected by the Coup in 1973 and purports to be museum of human rights. I had been looking forward to visiting the museum for some time but found it thoroughly disappointing. It is located much further from the city centre than most other key attractions in Santiago. The bureaucrats who made the Junta work are now apparently thriving in the new role as administrators to the Museo de la Memoria. Firstly you cannot take any photos – not just a restriction of flash photography – a ban on all photographs !! No reason is given – it is apparently just because the Museo Junta can impose such a ludicrous rule !! Secondly they purport to be focussed on communicating the abuse internationally – but everything is in Spanish only. You can pay for a translation headset, but the commentary is a monotone and the management manage to make what should be very interesting exhibits – DREARY. Once again because they can. Thirdly, there is no information about how those involved in the key abuses have be brought to justice – one assumes because they have not been punished. As Chile still operates under the Constitution imposed by the Junta, I guess that is to be expected. To me the Museo de la Memoria was a very disappointing and disillusioning exhibit, and a sign of the weakness of democracy in Chile today. Unless you are flush for time, do not bother with the Museo de la Memoria Chile.

review_text: We had a great tour of William Cole Vineyards today, quite by accident! We got lost on our way to another winery and ended up here. Javiera was our guide and she was wonderful. She answered all our many questions. Even though we had no reservations, they were happy to accommodate us. The tour took us into the vineyard, into fermentation building, and gave us a close-up look of the bottling process, something we haven't found anywhere else. Also, the tasting included delicious local cheeses. In all, we were very impressed by the vineyard, the winery, the tasting, the wines, and the guide. Our tour ended up being private which made it that much more personal. The facilities were also quite beautiful. I would definitely recommend a tour here. Some of the other vineyards spin a better tale (much of which simply doesn't jive with the reality of wine-growing/wine-making), but William Cole gives you more of a sense of the modern realities of a vineyard and wine-making.

review_text: We’ve done a lot of wine tourism, and normally arrange most of our own bookings. But since we were unfamiliar with the lay of the land and only had a short window to visit, we made a last minute decision to enlist the help of Connie and Farancisco. This turned out to be a really good decision. Connie answered emails almost immediately, and put together a day log itinerary that was perfect, including helping to rearrange restaurant reservations. Online payment very easy/straightforward. Francisco picked us up at our Posada outside of Santa Cruz and took us to 3 very different styles of wineries. While driving, he provided a nice local perspective of the area and the Chilean wine industry. Lunch at Fuegos de Apalta was a leisurely 2 hour treat before moving on to our last stop. We thoroughly enjoyed the day and the company. We would highly recommend CWT for any wine enthusiast visiting the area.

review_text: It is an amazing place a few minutes from San Pedro, you can even go renting a bike. The landscape is trully amazing, the colours and the salt cristal surrounding the dunes makes a very unique place to visit. Climb the big dune and take a look from there to the valley. There is an easy walking trail to go up. Nice sunset ! You can also go through the trail between the rocks that leads to the salt caverns. Interesting formations covered by salt cristals, many times covered with dust or sand you don't realize all the beautifull tiny little cristals along the way, pay atention pour some water and they shine unveiled. The cave is very narrow and although it has some openings to the open sky, I feel if you are claustrofobic is not a good idea to go in, you don't have to go in for doing the trail so do it, it is fun and interesting Where you park for seing Tres Marías ( a rock formation ) you can see the big cristals you are standing or parking if you place your atention to the floor. I pour some water and I enjoy looking at the cristal I was standing on.

review_text: Did the 6 day trip to the fjords with Juanfe, the owner/operator, who has been running trips for a long time. The difference with him as compared to other groups is his deep relationships with the local residents who live and work in the area of Pumalin and north Patagonia. He is a true outdoorsman and tells it like it is, so if you want more of a posh/comfy experience, then another outfitter might be better. Some of the other companies have supply/chase boats and in principle he is against the idea, because it changes the whole experience, and I agree. The area we visited is rugged and beautiful and conditions change rapidly; fortunately we were in good physical shape and had good gear, but we could have polished our skills in dealing with choppy water, wind and currents. Best time on the trip was interacting with the local Chileans who live in the area and let us stay with them in a Patagonian downpour and made the whole trip so much richer and authentic. A great time, you just need to be prepped for real wilderness and getting wet! Juanfe has a complete what-to-bring list and the kayaks are in great shape. Paying via western union and cash took a bit of extra effort, but went through just fine.

review_text: We took a boat trip early one morning to the Bernardo O'Higgins National Park to see the Balmaceda and Serrano Glaciers. It was a lovely way to spend the day. On the way up the fjords we passed some wildlife and smaller glaciers. Our catamaran took us to the park where we disembarked and walked up near to, the glacier with our guide passing a beautiful frozen lake on the way. We were rewarded with a pisco or whisky on the rocks when we returned to the catamaran. After our trip to the park we were back on our catamaran and off to lunch at an estancia where we had barbecued lamb before making our way back to Puerto Natales. The scenery was amazing, it was a great trip and good value for money. I would definitely recommend this if you have time when in Puerto Natales.

Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago Hello Sorry for not having fulfilled your expectations. I agree that is impossible have enough time to visit Valparaiso in a 1 day tour because is too much to see for excemple the ascensors (Funiculars) that are around 30 in the city. We take one or two that is enough to experience it because as you said is many more things to see and is not possible go up and down in ascensor in the walking tour. The idea of the tour is give you a good idea of the concept of Valparaiso, and see the most interesting places without waste time getting lost that is so easy there. Is very common that people which before visit Valparaiso though that is a small costal village and is not like that. This is a 600,000 people city the 3rd largest in Chile. About lunch it not exist a cheap or expensive side. In Valparaiso is hygienic or unhygienic. If you go to a restaurant not matter where is located, pretty side or no pretty side as in middle of a fish market it will be the same price, minimum USD $20 per person. In other hand you have the ''picadas'' where the fishermen, the man which park cars eat which cost USD $10 but this is good for people which live there and will not get sick with any of that food but you that are new in the area will have a big risk to get sick. So our decision is easy that is recommend you a safety place to eat. The tasting is not long but not as short as you sentence. Why is not long is because this is a costal tour in which we want to give an extra that's why we included a visit to a winery without take too much time of the Valparaiso and Viña del Mar tour. review_text: Chile Off Track arranged for Barbara (not then listed on their website) to conduct a private tour for two of us at a time (1300-1800) other than advertised at just one day’s notice. We were collected from our hotel and the tour was interesting (mainly walking). We felt our lack of knowledge of Santiago meant there was a disconnect between our expectations and outcome as we were asked if there was anything specific we wanted to see, which we were unable to answer. There was a chance to visit the inside of a building (Museum?) in the Plaza de Armas (admission presumably not included) but we felt this was an inappropriate use of our time with our guide and we didn’t want to miss out on whatever we were supposed to be seeing There were access restrictions in place in some areas of the city causing traffic and itinerary issues On the tour with the published times a snack and a drink are included but on this non standard tour we had the opportunity to buy our own snack only, although a coffee at a very interesting cafe was provided. One big plus in these fraught times for Santiago was that our guide was fluent in Spanish and local awareness, meaning we felt entirely safe in her company. After the tour we were driven back to our hotel Overall Much safer than doing it yourself and we are glad we did the tour If you are better prepared than we were you may not carry the feeling that somehow you missed out on something unknown Review of: Santiago City Highlights Walking Tour - Private Half Day

review_text: We have just returned from Patagonia. Travelling on the Navimag ferry from Puerto Natales to Puerto Montt was the second last part of our trip. Overall, it was a good experience as it gave us time to contemplate the mountainous landscape of Southern Chili. Unfortunately, the skies were gray, the weather rainy, cold and windy during most of the 3 day trip. No beautiful sunrise or sunset on the water for us, as per Navimag’s publicity. We had our binoculars with us which allowed us to contemplate the seabirds and one colony of sea lions on a rock. Unfortunately, to see whales, one should plan one’s trip when the whales move to the inner passage during breeding season. Over 3 days, only a couple of dolphins were seen briefly swimming in the distance. Navimag’s uses images of wildlife in its publicity but sightings depends on many factors above and beyond its control. Also, to benefit from announcements about the geography, animal life or even limitations due to the weather, the sound system should be substantially improved. The staff was very good at keeping clean the environment which is a challenge considering that the ferry is over 30 years old and lacks many modern features. The kitchen staff would benefit from an expanded base of recipes for food preparation. Navimag’s publicity of fresh vegetables and other colorful dishes does not correspond to the reality of a starch and meat diet where salt is the main seasoning. Also, replacing sachet Nescafé coffee by freshly brewed coffee, at least in the morning, could be an added element of hospitality. Although the ferry has a local network for the distribution of films and games, only the captain has access to internet and cellphone services which can become an issue in times of delays. Navimag’s information should contain some indication that delays are part of travelling at sea. Our date of departure was delayed twice, the first time many days before and the second time the day just before leaving. For individuals, like ourselves, who had booked transportation for the next leg of our trip long before, based on the given information, this became a serious issue, in terms of time, cost and additional stress. Our advice would be to consider departure-arrival times given by Navimag as “flexible” and book accordingly by leaving at least 2 days of leg time each way. Luckily enough, we made it for our flight from Puerto Montt to Santiago in time to be with friends and enjoy the seaside. As individuals working in tourism in Chile, they were quick to mention that a 5 star price should reflect a 5 star experience but that sometimes, this was not always the case in Chile, Navimag being one example of this situation.

review_text: I wanted to let you know of my recent experience with your service. On July 5 my boyfriend arrived in Chile so around 11am I went online to try to buy two Hop On Hop Off tickets at the discounted rate. My order was stuck in pending status for an hour so we went to your counter at Costanera Center to address it. The on-site staff informed us he couldn’t assist in any way. I asked if there was someone he could call, but he said there wasn't, so we just waited till the order changed status. I tried a second time and that order failed. At that point I was forced to pay the full rate with the on-site staff. We ended up getting on the bus at 1pm, only 5 hours left in the pass. My only comfort was that I had purchased the 2-day so we’d be able to come back another day f we missed anything. When we tried to board the first bus, we learned my boyfriend’s wristband did not have the QR code printed on it. We were told no one could help us so we'd just need to explain what had happened to any staff we encountered. As it turns out, we had delays everywhere we went. I’m sure the overall delays amounted to at least 30 minutes, especially trying to get around the teleférico and funicular, since we had to explain the situation over and over again to have someone override the system and let us through. In other words, even more time was stolen from the few hours we had left of your service. I need to highlight that the staff on the buses and on location were very good. The next day my dad woke up sick (I live in the US and am visiting Chile to help him with his cancer treatment). I wasn’t able to leave the house till early afternoon so we went to Turistik in Parque Arauco to get my boyfriend’s wristband fixed and use it the following day. We were informed that the two days had to be back to back. I explained the situation with my dad and was told the second day was just a courtesy and had no value. I told him that we needed it since we started very late the day before. Your staff said that was my choice to start late. There was absolutely no consideration for my father’s health or the multiple issues we had faced. I was honestly shocked. I expected better customer service from a company geared towards tourists. How hard was it to give us that extra day given that it's low season and the buses were relatively empty? Por eso no entendemos como fue que nunca supiste a quien ubicar o a quien llamar para hablar sobre tu caso de compra on-line. La compra en nuestro infocenter del mall, fue decisión propia, pudiste volver a comprar on-line para obtener el descuento. A su vez, en toda nuestra folletería, web y demás medios, están explícitas nuestras políticas y normativa de cada servicio. review_text: We took this ferry in March from Puerto Natales to Puerto Montt. It certainly is a mixed bag of good and quite bad. The bad: The ferry was three days late. You want a flexible schedule if you are taking this. The day you board you have to get your luggage to their office ahead of time. When we finally boarded we stayed in port overnight (routine) while they loaded the cargo. We did not leave until late afternoon the next day. On our final morning we docked at about 8 am so you spend four nights on board for two days of sailing on top of being tied up the day of boarding because you have to deliver your luggage. It is very expensive, charging cruise ship prices for a barely adequate ferry. We paid about $600 US each. This gives you four nights (one in port) and less than three full days. The food is adequate but not at all exciting. They even rationed the coffee (instant.) The room was satisfactory. We had an inside with no toilet or shower. The male toilets backed up frequently. The housekeeping and kitchen staff did not put themselves out at all and we left no tip at the end. Because the ferry was late, we sailed by some of the best sights at night and did not see the glacier coming down to the water. The ship is a utilitarian ferry and not well designed for tourists. The one dining room and lounge both looked out to starboard so we could only see views in one direction through dirty windows unless we ventured outside. There was no entertainment except for a TV room which was mainly used by truck drivers and local passengers watching pre-broadcast football (soccer) games. There was an English speaking lecturer and he was quite interesting though he seemed bored with his job. Neutral: there were at least two open containers with cattle (about 15 per container.) They were cramped but did not crush each other. There was a worker onboard who watered and fed them each day. The smell was not bad at all. The good: We got to understand the vast emptiness of Patagonia. In the two full days of sailing we went by one tiny village and a few salmon farms. The rest is islands, mountains (some snow peaked) and water. It was very pretty, but having just been to Antarctica, it was similar but not so spectacular. We had lots of time to relax. Thank goodness we are readers and had books for there was little else to do. If I were doing this again I would take the bus through Argentina (which I hear has improved a bit) or fly. However if you have lots of time then you could consider the ferry.

When we finished he gave us very clear instructions on routes to take back to our hotel and areas to absolutely avoid later in the day. We did as he suggested and had no problems. This was one of the most unusual city bike tours we’ve even taken and one of the most memorable. Highly recommended.

review_text: My girlfriend and I extensively researched the different travel agencies in San Pedro de Atacama offering 3D/2N salt flats tours. As many have experienced before us, its more than a little overwhelming with all the options! In the end we decided on Towanda Tours because of the lovely german & chilian couple that ran the office (they have at least 4 offices in San Pedro). They were completely honest about what their tour included and explained that they were one of the few agencies that owned their own jeeps (there are many agencies that simply organise and then once you get to the Bolivian border you are placed in another companies jeep). We were expecting them to cost more so were delighted when they said their price was just 95,000 Chilean pesos which was one the cheapest we had found. They are also one of the few operators who take the EASTERN route on the whole of the 2nd day (the first day and third day are identical to the Western route). This suited us as you sleep at lower altitude in a town called Villamar which means less chance of altitude sickness (although we didn't really suffer from this) and warmer at night. The second day was great, we saw lots of things that were not available on the western route (I suggest going there to get the full details). Couldn't fault the accommodation in Villamar or in the salt hostel on the second night (didn't bother showering for 3 days even though there was the option at the salt hostel so be prepared for that!) The food was fantastic and much larger quantities than we expected. We advise you bring snacks but we didn't nearly need as many as we thought. As with all the drivers our driver spoke very little English but you aren't going to find any agencies with English drivers as by law they have to be Bolivian. He was friendly enough and a very good driver which is the important thing! Our jeep was a bit slower than the other 2 jeeps in our convoy but this didn't bother us much as we got on really well with the other 4 people in our jeep. Thanks Towanda for an epic and unforgettable experience!

review_text: We visited both the valleys with Cosmo Andino (detailed TA review on their page) around sunset. Both the valleys are quite different in the colour of their soil/sand. In the death valley or Mars Valley, the sand had a reddish tinge. The way the forces of nature had eroded the landscape and carved majestic symmetrical patterns in the rocks over hundreds of thousands of years was quite astonishing. We had the opportunity to run down massive sand-dunes which were a whole lot of fun. One might spot the odd beetle or two. There were some interesting desert plants that I saw as well. Valley of the moon was incredible! The entire landscape was peppered with white dust and it did resemble something from outer-space. We saw the three Marias although only two exist now and the natural amphitheatre. The story behind the three Marias or the stars of the Orion belt believed to be protectors for the natives (as told by our guide) was quite intriguing. From the top of the sand-dunes in the Moon Valley, we had an incredible view of the landscape. As the sun set, the changing colours of the sand was quite incredible. Tips ------ 1. Wear sturdy hiking boots. 2. Carry sunglasses and a broad-brimmed hat. 3. Best to carry some water too. 4. Since there will be lots of toursits at these sites, it would be best to be quick with your photos.

review_text: We were 4 days with Juan paddling in Pulalin Park beginning of September 2015. Juan was very responsive and diligent in preparing us for this kayaking trip. He paid attention to the details including food restrictions. His wife cooked e.g. vegetarian food for my daughter and he brought Nutella as a surprise for breakfast. The trip is an adventure and admittedly it was physically more demanding than we expected. This was our first Kayak trip. We were super lucky with the weather but it was at times quite cold. You really need good sleeping bags in winter. The Northern Patagonia Fjord was magical especially in the early morning and late at night. Meeting Senora Nora was very special. She is a 86 year old local institution who cooked for us, who warmed us after freezing paddling tours and gave us lovely insights in how it is to live in Patagonia. Juan is full of stories and passionate about Patagonia and the people living here. We always felt safe and Juan made also flipping the Kayak as security training fun. He only had difficulties to adjust to our speed. While we asked him that we have a preference to stay together it was difficult for him to not paddle away. He was so much faster in comparison to us.

review_text: The best part of the tour was not getting to Cajon del Maipo itself, but getting to meet our guide, Francisco. His love for Chile, adventure, and travel is palpable right from the beginning. Right when you get into his van in Santiago, he tells you interesting stories and facts about the city. He seems to know absolutely everything about Santiago and the Andes. He is excited when he tells you his stories and is just happy you're there to listen. You feel safe in his van, even though the rocky mountain roads and takes you farther than into the mountains than any other tour group. We went on a day with beautiful weather to Cajon Del Maipo where the sun shone brightly, the winds were calm, and there was not a hint of cloudy skies. The lake was turquoise green and quite the sight to see. I recommend climbing a big rock along the shore away from the crowds and simply enjoy the scenery and the blessing it is to be in a place so beautiful. After an hour or so of self-exploring, Francisco prepared a beautiful picnic for us with red wine, cheese, and snacks. I realized that even though Cajon del Maipo is a sight to behold, the true gift is getting to know the soul of Chile. Francisco embodies that. There is so much excitement and love in this human being that it's contagious. By the end of the trip, you'll also be in love with Chile and Santiago and wish you could stay forever. Review of: Cajon Del Maipo Including Wine with Picnic and Empanada

review_text: Amazing rock and sand formations that have resulted from volcanic activity and years of post-volcanic erosion. The terrain feels like outer space. For the more intrepid there is a semi-difficult trek on a narrow rocky path which gives excellent views. But easier trails also lead to the best viewing points. review_text: As a mother of 3 adult children, planning an rare opportunity for all of us to be together and do an active vacation in Chile was a bit daunting until I connected with Cristian at EcotoursChile. He helped select the hotels, how much time to spend in each place, and guided us to the best place to do hiking and biking during the April time frame. The trip was fantastic and well beyond all of our expectations! What do you think when you are going to a Desert for 6 days? Well, it is a desert but the geography, climate at different elevations, ecological impact of the flooding and mining, the lush valleys, many wildlife (even saw a fresh puma footprint!) are just a few of the learnings you will have. Our guides were outstanding Daniel. Marco and Mariano. All of them went well beyond by providing lots of education, new hiking routes that were so scenic (I ended up taking 468 pictures!), crazy fun and challenging biking routes (that even I tried!). They organized an spontaneous birthday party for us to see the sunset! The stayed up late and educated us on stargazing! So, I would highly recommend this company and team. Our hotel in Valparaiso was fantastic overlooking the ocean, the service impeccable and our hotel in Atacama was just what you need when hiking and biking. The laundry was included and much to my surprise - we used it alot - red dust everywhere! Bottom line- fantastic holiday! My kids were so pumped! Thank you to all at Ecotours Chile for making it so fabulous. We will be back to do South Chile next! The only thing I would ask for next time is a suggested packing list!

review_text: Wanted to go hiking to the park for a day trip and were not disappointed! Even though most routes were closed on that specific day due to bad (slightly rainy) weather, the hike to the lakes (lagos) was open. Essentially the walk consists of going up the hill, enjoying nice views over the big lake at the entrance and the volcano across (assuming few clouds) and then the 3 small lakes on the top, a small break and then down the same route. There are 3 or so buses a day from Pucon and we took the first one at 7:30am. We would definitely recommend that as the small crowd draws out rather quickly and you have much time hiking by yourself while in the afternoon on our way down, quite a few people were coming up including small groups.

review_text: If you, like me, enjoy cemeteries as time capsules of art, history, and culture, visit. -You can walk here from the city center in 15 minutes -If you do not wish to walk, there is a taxi rank right outside -The window at the entry says there is an admission fee, but it was not collected either time I visited. -The cemetery has a good mix of traditional and elaborate mausoleums, memorials to social groups (indigenous peoples, prisoners who disappeared under Pinochet, the Red Cross, etc.) and typical South American crypts/drawers that are very decorated. -The foliage is also interesting and well kept. -You can really see the town's diversity in all the names and decorations on the graves - everything from Croatian names and sheep statues to Nicaraguan political posters. -It is a quiet, beautiful place perfect for reflection. Please visit, learn, and be respectful when you photograph (I saw people who were a bit over the top.) Keep in mind that the deceased still have frequent visitors, who may feel a bit upset at you using your selfie stick in front of Abuelita's tomb.

review_text: We did three different tours with Colque Tours. My understanding is there are two main tour companies and then many subcontractors that you book the tour with and they assign you to one of the tour companies that will get your guide ready..... Tour 1- Valle de la Luna in San Pedro- this was a great tour with a bilingual guide. We did a lot more than I was told we would. Tour 2- lagunas escondidas/ Laguna baltinache. We were told to only bring swimsuits, so NOBODY on the tour bought jackets except me because I'm always over prepared. It was very cold, but the lagunas were worth it. Tour 3- SALAR DE UYUNI, 3 days&2nights. First off- the our started 1.5 hours late. This was a decent tour, bc we had a decent guide. He only spoke Spanish & seemed to hate his job. Not a problem for us, just something to be aware of. Our guide was nice. However! Beware!! Colque Tours told us that we wouldn't need to pay a visa into Bolivia & that we would be fine to go with the tour. Well first stop at the border, we have to pay $160 each for a visa. It's okay bc I had read that we would, so we brought extra money just in case. If you are a US citizen, pay in bolivianos bc they CHECK USD for any little sign of wear/tear. The tour overall was good but I'm disappointed in the company we signed up with not only for the visa problem but also because we missed the arbol de piedra because the lady lied and said we would see it all, but in reality we would have had to take an additional tour. Go with a different company !

review_text: this coffee shop is a real gem. The place is a high-quality coffee shop with delicious pastries sandwiches, and a wide selection of hot and cold beverages, with the added twist that the coffee shop is filled with cats. These cats are all adopted and they are calmly circulating around the different areas of the coffee shop. The place is very strict on the rules necessary for the cats not to be disturbed by the presence of the customers while allowing for a wonderful interaction between the cats and the customers. The food, and the service alone is worth a visit, and when you add that counts to the mix, the place becomes absolutely irresistible. I recommend going by taxi, walking or using an Uber rather than going by car because this is located in our rather busy area in Santiago where parking is almost impossible and they are plenty of municipal officers roaming around ready to give you a parking ticket . That issue aside, you are in for a lovely experience. To attend you must reserve in advance detailing how many adults and children will be going, and you will be requested to pay a reservation fee . This fee is afterwards deducted from the overall of your bill. I went with my grandmother and my son and they both loved it and we will definitely be going again. Many times soon. I highly recommend it!!

review_text: I highly recommend Atacama Desert Stargazing. Jorge and his finance were super friendly, knowledgeable, and generous with their time and energy. They picked us up at the airport and spent the day touring us around tiny desert villages and secret spots before ending up at the Tatio Geyser Field where the rustic base camp was located. A delicious dinner with Chilean wine was served and enjoyed with the 4 wardens on duty, who soon crashed asleep in preparation for the busloads of tourists that arrive at 5-6am the next morning (Tatio geysers is one of the most popular tours from San Pedro). The astronomy tour takes place outside under the sky in comfy chairs with blankets around 10-12pm, aided by laser and telescope viewing. You can stay out all night and photograph to your heart's content (or until the bitter cold forces you inside!) There are 2 bunk rooms which guests share with the wardens (male and female rooms). And another perk? You can sleep in a little later the next morning before touring the geysers, as they are only a ten minute drive away! We asked to view them at 6:30am (the most active time for photography) but Jorge usually takes his guests much later after the busloads have disappeared. Breakfast follows before the long drive to San Pedro. Overall, the whole experience was my favorite in the Atacama Desert, and I thank Jorge for offering such an opportunity! Click here to see my photos with explanations: http://www.uniquetravelphoto.com/?p=2172 Dear Traveller, Thank you very much for your possitive and complete review. The option about SAT (Special Astronomical Tour) is simply awesome the altitude of the location in where we mounted the telescope is just be in another world the proximity of the stars, the low temperature make us feel and amazing view of the sky. For astrophotography this location is one of the best spot in where there are no car or normal light polution allowing us enjoy for a long time of the wonder of southern night sky. My Best Regards Jorge Corante F.

review_text: In late February we embarked on a 4 week journey to Chile. We combined some independent travel with guided tours using Cristian from Ecotours Chile for help with the planning and arrangements. That decision made this trip so much easier. We covered a lot of territory from the desert in northern Chile to trekking in Torres del Paine. Cristian organized our 8 day bike trip in the Lakes and Volcano region and our 5 day trek in Torres del Paine along with arrangements for extra days in Puerto Varas, Puerto Natalie’s and Santiago and the needed bus transfers to/from Torres del Paine. The bike trip was a bit of a stretch for us as we were mainly rails to trails bikers BUT so glad we pushed our boundaries. It was an amazing not to be missed experience. Our biking guide and support van driver were wonderful. Besides talking about what we were seeing and sharing insights they were alert to group or individual needs. The “W” trek in Torres del Paine was awe inspiring. We stayed in Refugios as we hiked along the trail. Yes, usually 6 person rooms but clean and comfortable with hot showers down the hall and dining facilities so you only need to carry your personal items for this 5 day trek. Pretty cushy trekking!!! Again our guide served us well, stopping to point out things of interest, providing insights into the local culture and even making fresh coffee for us in the morning. Chile is such a spectacular country and so diverse. You leave wanting to return for more. Our trip was fabulous and Cristian did an outstanding job putting it together and in his recommendations for our independent travel days. Thank you Cristian for taking such good care of us.

review_text: This excursion was the closest I got to trouble on the entire Atacama trip!! Bolivia's structure is nothing like Chilean gourmet food. The bathrooms (which you have to pay for) are precarious, the hostel on the 1st and 3rd day is very humble and you have to pay to use the towels (and no internet!!!!!). Taking this into consideration, take a deep breath and GO! I lack words to describe the beauty of everywhere! I recommend not taking too much, as the luggage goes on top of the car and you will share the vehicle with 6 other people (my group and I only took a carry-on backpack, dressed in 3 layers of clothes and with lots of toilet paper). At the back of the vehicle, there is a person and the food (the guide is responsible for all your food during the trip, he arrives at the place to prepare the food while you are walking and then everything is served. The food is wonderful! Best food of the entire trip - only on the last day did I discover that I ate llama meat for every meal)z Upon arriving in Bolivia, you will spend the day inside the Bolivian national park (it costs 150 Bolivianos and payment is mandatory and part of the tour). There's a geyser, a thermal pool, lagoons with a thousand flamingos, cold as hell, gloves and scarves flying everywhere!! And the altitude reaches 5000m. On the second day, there's a lagoon, rock formations and canyons, a ghost town, cactus beer, but we were less cold and with fewer layers of clothes. The third day is at Salar de Uyuni. We woke up early to leave the hostel and dawn on the salt flat. It was the most surprising experience of my life. Multimedia artifacts, including film, letters, newspaper headlines, and many photographs brought every aspect of this period into stark relief. A must for history buffs or anyone who wants to know more about this most significant period of Chilean history. It also features a wall dedicated to describing the human rights abuses that occurred - or are still occurring - in other countries throughout the world.

review_text: We took the ferry from Puerto Chacabuco. It is advertised as leaving at 18.00 and we were told to report for embarkation at 16.00. They load cargo first so at 18.15 we were still sitting waiting. We finally left at 21.00. We had calm weather and flat seas so should have arrived at 21.00 the next day but in fact did not dock until after 1.00. The gangway for passengers was stuck which caused more delay. We ended up climbing down steep stairs. Our hire car was waiting, bless him, but we had to pay a surcharge for late pick up. We spent the night in the car outside our hotel as there was no night porter. Airplanes were invented to save us from this torture. We did not expect much of the food but it was not good: yellow broccoli and apples with bad bits. Some nice views and a couple of whales did not make up for the horror. We're sorry that the trip did not live up to your expectations. We will take your feedback into consideration.

review_text: Very professional, instructive and fun. This particular company should be considered if you are thinking of an astronomical tour in the Atacama. I was picked up at around 21:15 hrs as promised in a small bus, typical of all the companies in this area. There were less than 20 people and we were taken out to a rural area on the outskirts of San Pedro. The explanations were in Spanish and English and were of the right length and detail for an amateur like me. The sky was amazing and the three telescopes were used to view some planets, Jupiter and Mars in our case, constellations and clusters. The evening was rounded off by drinks and snacks and finally time lapse photos of individuals and groups which were sent by email within 48 hrs. We were returned to our pick up points and in my case I was back at my Hotel by 01:00 hrs. Just right. What a wonderful way to expand your understanding of the universe and your place in it.

review_text: Phenomenal ship. Phenomenal crew. Phenomenal food. Phenomenal Antarctica. Now here are the details that I think people considering or about to take the trip would find helpful. On December 27, 2017, we congregated in the basement of the hotel where the company had set up shop to choose our boots. Everything was very smooth. We had ordered the Musto BR2 expedition jackets from the gear shop and they were shipped here. We had also ordered hats, socks, gloves. The gloves didn’t fit. The person there said the company can’t do anything about this, which upset us because the jackets were exchangeable for size and so should the gloves. Anyway it turned out this person had given us the wrong information. As expected, a well-run business should have many sizes in stock for its business. They did and the gloves were ultimately exchanged for the right sizes. Also we were given very high quality water proof duffel bags with company logo. Functional as well as a sentimental reminder of the great trip. You can put extras you don’t need in the duffel to leave at the hotel. We were supposed to fly out the next day in the morning but weather made it uncertain. We were placed on active wait and were told to check back at 2 pm. Turned out we could leave earlier and some people were caught off guard as they had gone off on local outings. Luckily they found out somehow and all was okay but keep in mind you have to be available to be contacted if plans change and they can change at any moment due to weather conditions. The company took us to a nice buffet lunch at the Dreams Hotel at the port. From there, all of us already dressed in our winter insulated pants, layers, jackets and boots got on the bus and off we went to the airport. Airline was good. We even got food for the two and a half hour trip. No need to pay extra for preferred seating. Definitely not worth it. The ship is a wonderful ship. Small and intimate, yet spacious enough that we never felt crowded. There is a common space on the upper deck; a library with great collection of travel and other books, and a cappuccino machine; and a little gym. The dining room is also open and welcoming. There were about 60 plus people on board so we could all disembark for our expeditions without having to take turns (due to the fact that there is a maximum number of people allowed to disembark per Antarctica rules. So if you are on a boat with 200 people for example, some would have to stay onboard while a first group gets off). Our boat can also go through ice without danger to the boat which makes navigating to different and difficult areas possible. The food was absolutely amazing. Breakfast lunch dinner. Nothing we can pick on. Selection of food, variety, quality, presentation, service. This was the case for appetizers, soup, dessert, bread, cheese spread. At dinner, there are food selections at the buffet as well as food that can be selected from the menu. All absolutely incredible. The crew was first class. Friendly. Eager. Smiling. Welcoming. Yet never intrusive. One evening we were even surprised with a fun and fabulous bbq on deck. Fish. Steak. Ribs. Lamb. All top quality. Our fellow travelers were a pleasure to be around. Almost everyone was a seasoned, cosmopolitan traveler. This isn’t surprising given the kind of trip this was. Adventure. Remote. A bit “exotic.” Hence most had been to many countries on every continent already before embarking on an Antarctica expedition. We enjoyed the fact that our paths crossed with theirs and we have many friends we continue to be in touch with. Our room was a triple room with a bunk bed that sleeps two and a regular twin bed. There are details that deserve mention. Mattresses were good and firm. Bathroom had shower with good water pressure. There is a dispenser for combined shower gel, shampoo and conditioner. It was good but if you want extra conditioner, bring your own. We were provided with slippers and bathrobes. Room was equipped with hair dryer as well as an electrical “octopus” so you can charge multiple devices. You do need to bring your own electrical plugs as the outlets are the round ones used in South America. Each bunk bed had its own dark curtains to block out light. Antarctica itself was beyond wonderful. Each expedition will be different because which island or cliff you visit will be dependent on weather, wind, ice, movement of glaciers etc. But we loved every part that we visited. The first day it was very very cold and windy with heavy snow coming down. We saw gentoo penguins and had plenty of time to explore and sit still as well to observe their behavior. We were but 6 inches away from many of them. The next day we visited a colony of Adelie penguins and later, chin strap penguins. We saw different types of seals such as leopard seals. Saw lots of whales from the dining room as well. Apart from the animal sightings, it was also very special to be immersed in the environment itself, the all-enveloping pristine whiteness, the remoteness of geography, separate from us but a part of us as well. The company is very well-run. Everything went smoothly. The boat, again, is a great boat chartered by Antarctica xxi for Antarctica expeditions. The same boat (with the wait staff and hotel crew) apparently is then chartered by another company to do Arctic expeditions as well. I think this boat is just the perfect balance between intimate and spacious, adventure and luxury. We signed up for kayaking. The group is a maximum of ten. It fills up quickly so do sign up early if you want to kayak. Also once you do kayak, then you can no longer get your money back if you change your mind. And additional thing to keep in mind is the fact that you do get to kayak, weather permitting, twice a day. There is always time for you to ALSO do a regular visit on land with the rest of the boat after your kayak stint. If you choose not to kayak and opt for just a land based visit with others not kayaking, your spot cannot be given to someone else just for that day. I do think there is a way to accommodate more people to kayak if the company is willing to change the rules. It’s very doable. Just let people on the wait list come to the orientation. They can pick out and be fitted for their kayaking outfit and gear. And they can be slotted in and pay to kayak if a regular opts out of a session. There were people eager to kayak who didn’t get the chance even though some of us did not kayak every available opportunity. There was also a snow shoe group, also limited in size. Again sign up early if you want to snow shoe. Our group left January 2, 2018. I know some of us wanted uncooperative weather so we would be “stuck” on board. The night before our last day, we were treated to a slide show of our expedition. Beautiful photographs had been taken by Krystle, our photographer. She had also compiled a travel log which contains all the details of the places that we visited. Slide show photos and trip log were available on the website that we would have access to. Forgot to mention the crazy polar plunge which I did. Yippie. Cold but worth it. Very safe in our harness. What else can we say? It’s an exhilarating, exciting expedition. Worth every moment and every expensive penny. Highly recommend. Please remember to tip the boat crew, most from the Philippines, and the expedition staff.

review_text: My wife, friend, and I hit up Last Hope distillery as our night cap for the final day of our trip through Chilean Patagonia. After a long 5 day backpacking trip we were beyond surprised to find such a well established, although relatively young bar. The bar was packed but they had outdoor seating with blankets and cushions to keep patrons warm. The Australian owner was a pleasant surprise for us English speakers and greeted our table with a tasting of both of their gins. The traditional dry-London gin was a strong and delicious sharp gin with local Chilean botanicals, making it unique from any of your popular northwestern dry gins. The Calafate gin was a huge, welcome change of pace that was a deep purple from the Calafate berry they steep the gin with. For those that aren't as into the dry gins this alternative was perfect. The Calafate gimlet compliments the tart berry with the sour citrus flavors, making an amazing combination that you can enjoy all night. The service was stellar, always with full water glasses, something I personally appreciate at a bar. The atmosphere pulled us completely out of the rural Patagonia mountains into a city speakeasy cushioned booth. For those that needed some eats, they served some great shareable plates from bread pudding with local vanilla Gelato to roasted nuts. 10/10 wish we could've stayed longer and tried every drink and their whiskey that's still in the first barrel.

review_text: Tour Guide: Antonia This is THE way to get to know the city of Santiago, its culture, its people and its modern history, in the shortest amount of time. I only had 2 days in Santiago, so did not expect to really get a chance to know its culture and feel a sense of the hearts of its people. However, I was completely blown away by Antonia's ability to take elements of the city such as buildings, murals, bars and even doorknobs(!) and incorporate them into the tour and into her narrative in a way that symbolically epitomised myriad elements of Santiago's and Chile's history, culture and society. Antonia has true passion for what she does and she conveyed that passion to the group in every stop we made. The tour touches on a variety of elements of Chile's culture and history, including (of course) Spanish colonialism and later independence, then things as varied as the reasons for the large amount of stray dogs in Santiago, the existence of elitist clubs in the commerce district and the co-existence of an anti-thetical bar right next door, descriptions of the beautiful street art by artists like Inti Castro, with real depth of interpretation of the artist's intentions and how the murals relate to Chile's culture. The highlights for me were the discussions of September 11, 1973 and Salvador Allende's legacy and fall. Which has affected me for the rest of my life. I highly recommend this tour to anyone travelling to Santiago. It is a must do. If you're lucky enough to get Antonia as a guide, then even more so.

review_text: The house, history behind it, and of course Pablo Neruda are all interesting, but I'm sorry to say that after touring the house I didn't really have a feeling for who Pablo Neruda was or for the "real feel" of the house. The audio guided tour did say a lot, but it didn't seem all that informative - didn't reveal much. I left La Chascona feeling like I didn't get a real sense for who Pablo Neruda was - and that's very odd for touring someone's home - where you're supposed to learn all of those types of things. We left not having learned anything about Pablo Neruda's extended family (just the wives/mistresses) or even intimate details about his life. For example, I don't know if he ever had any children during his life - the whole topic was entirely forgotten by this museum - there are many other examples. We're pleased we went and learned what we did, but I am blown away that Trip Advisor has rated this the 2nd most popular site in Santiago - far from it...

review_text: There were many things to like about this experience: our host, Inez, was lovely and shared a lot of helpful information, the food was great, the drinks were delicious and plentiful, and the participants were a fun and varied group of people from all over the world. On the other hand...there were 13 of us, which felt like about two times bigger than it should have been for us to have a meaningful cooking class. The size of the group meant that each person could only really focus on one task (in my case, chopping tomatoes, which isn't really particular to Chilean cuisine!). It was also way, way, way too many people to bring to the market in one group and still have everyone be able to participate in the tour -- which was unfortunate, since visiting a market is usually one of the most fun and interesting parts of a local cooking class. There are some ways to avoid this issue, of course -- like booking a private class or trying to book on a less popular day. But I also think the folks who run the course should seriously consider shifting the class limit to 6 if they really want people to come away feeling that they've had a chance to learn how to cook Chilean food. Another option would be to have more than one chef / guide lead the market tour and/or cooking. On balance, it was a fun and interesting way to learn a bit about Chilean cuisine and to try a number of different dishes -- but given the limitations of having so many people involved, I felt it was more of an enhanced dining experience than a cooking class. Still recommended, but not quite what we were hoping for.

review_text: Very impressive museum about Chile recent history. Very moving: September 11th has a special meaning in Chile. It was on 9/11/1973 that the democratically-elected government of socialist Salvador Allende was overthrown in a bloody coup. Thus began for the Chilean people, a dark period of repression and civil rights violations including mass torture and murder under the Pinochet's dictatorship. The museum is very well designed. The first floor has a variety of video screens in the center which present footage of the siege of the presidential palace. Further back in an enclosed area, there are personal recounts on the different types of tortures. Along the sides of each floor is press coverage of what happened during these years, along with response from around the world expressing solidarity with the Chilean people. The exhibit ends toward the far end of the 3rd floor with video of the 1988 plebiscite that led to the eventual restoration of democracy in Chile. Although Pinochet was legally pursued for the numerous crimes committed during his rule, he managed to avoid incarceration and died peacefully at age 91 in Santiago. We owe it to those who suffered to remember.

For me this is crazy to tip a guide $20 each. First of all in a country where the average wage is $500 per month he would have earned $400 for 2.30h this is crazy. Now he did speak about history but also about how American influence had messed with the Chilean economy in the past and those influences are still in society today that the people are protesting to change and for someone whom promotes socialism it seems very hypocritical that they would ask for so much in tips. Now I understand that I was only suggested but it’s very awkward at the start of the tour I would recommend that the company does not offer to say any amount and let the people decided. For the quality and length of the tour I would only give $5 as we had over 20 people in the group and he would have earned $100 that is more than fair in Chile. Hi TravelwithCarlo, Sorry that your experience with our tour team was not great. You are completely in your right to determine what you want to give based on the quality of the outing. Regarding our team and Chile income, we do not have a tour payment minimum, but we do have an average and that is what everyone asks our guides, so we do share that information just like we share the year a building was constructed before customers ask. Regarding the average wage in Chile, it is over 800 USD and unfortunately it is not enough for a decent standard of living, which is why Chile has the highest disproportionate income between rich and poor. Thanks again for your feedback. Contact us via email and we will happily make up for the average experience you had with us. Sincerely, Peter

review_text: We spent five wonderful days in south of Chile, with our two Andes-Explora guides. We initially met to discuss our preferences and they custom-designed our trip, for an incredible adventure in some of the most remotes and beautiful natural landscapes that we had ever seen. We fully enjoyed sharing the time with these smart, knowledgeable, energetic and passionate young men, who are both professionals (a lawyer and an economist) that followed their passion and created a company to show and share nature in its purest form. Be prepared to be flexible with the schedule, since the changes in weather are extreme. The accommodations may vary from a luxurious lodge with gourmet food, to sharing a house and meals with a local family, with very simple and rustic accommodations . Our trip included traveling by truck sometimes in dirt roads, kayaking, hiking and boat trips. We are forever grateful for this experience and for the wonderful memories. Thank you Tomás and Matías, for a great adventure. Thanks a lot for your feedback Renzo! Was nice to meet you. Your are an amazing couple with a great pasion for the wild nature. keep that ability to be amazed by the nature. Was very nice travel with you and María del Carmen, along the beautiful green Patagonia. We hope to see you again in new Andes Explora adventures. Matías

review_text: We used this company for three of our excursions in the Atacama Desert. We did Altiplanic Lagoons on the morning of 7/6, Valle de Luna in the afternoon on 7/6 and the Geysirs del Tatio on 7/7. For the Altilanic Lagoons, we arrived at the Flamenco National Reserve early before the other buses which was great because many flamingos were out and we could observe them before they flew away. We had three separate guides for each one and all of them were amazing! For some of our tours we were the only English speakers but our guides were bilingual and thoroughly explained everything in Spanish and English. The nature in this area was unreal and unlike anything we have ever seen before. Our guides were great in giving us fascinating information. All three locations were special and offered unique, beautiful landscape to observe. You leave very early for the lagoons and geysir tours and it was very cold outside. You definitely need to dress properly for the weather though the amazing views can help distract from the cold.

review_text: If you need a simple yet charming introduction to Valparaiso, you can't do better than Paseo Dimalow. First off, find your way to Ascensor Reina Victoria (the bottom end is at Elías Street, just off Cumming). If you're very thirsty or curious, you can always have a drink at the great Cervecería Altamira just before boarding. Then once you've paid your $100 (about 0.16 USD), you'll find yourself admiring the views of Valpo on your way up. Paseo Dimalow will instantly greet you with a wine bar, a playful slide, and local artists selling their wares. Now for drink and food, you have your pick between Fauna (my favorite) and its breathtaking views, the extension across the paseo called El Internado (great indoor space) or Taulat, among many other fine dining spots. Once you're done with this intense concentration of offers in one single street, you're well on your way to Cerro Alegre, which extends way beyond. Just do as everyone does and wander around, follow your instincts! Welcome to my not so secret Valparaiso.

review_text: Connie responded quickly and was able to accommodate our short notice reservations. We did the morning tour which allowed us to explore the markets with her while she explained the different foods and their use. We weren't rushed as we were able to buy coffee and some of our own grocery items. It just happened to be two of us on the tour, granted it's the off season for tourism. She did a great job explaining tips and things to know while going through the markets, and was very willing to answer any questions. We then took a short taxi ride to their kitchen they have in a residential area. There we made a Salsa to couple with pisco sour. We moved right into making flan, empanadas, cerviche and a rendition of a shepherd's pie but with a mashed sweet corn topping (the Chilean name isn't coming to mind.) I was greatful that we were able to still make traditional dishes dispite my gluten intolerance. I had the sweet corn dish while my boyfriend had the empanadas. Bam! We also enjoyed getting a preview of wine tasting. She paired our meals with wine and gave us a some additional information about them. Overall, excellent experience. Plus, we got aprons. Whoa. Awesome.
