review_text: I have a bias, I have been to Kingston Family Vineyards before and even got to meet and chat with Courtney's husband, so I am a big fan of the Kingston's and their wine. In fact, we have been wine club members for two years (free tour for club members) and have found them to wonderful to work with and Courtney's blogs about life and tourism in Chile are must-reads. So, when I knew we were going to Valparaiso with our Chilean friends, I suggested a tour of the Kingston Vineyard. This was a brave act on my part because one of our friends is very knowledgeable about wine. Eliana was great in handling the arrangements via email. We were met by our American guide, Beth, who greeted us with glasses of wine. It was a wonderful light and well-balanced Sauvignon Blanc. Beth was knowledgeable, articulate and enthusiastic. I felt like we were touring with an old friend. Even though I had been there before, I learned a lot more this time. This was a more in depth tour than when you are on a tour visiting several vineyards. The tour ended with a tasting of 3 more wines, which well chosen to demonstrate the range of wines they produce. This vineyard is very user friendly for Americans. It seems like everyone speaks English and buying their wine in the US is easier than getting it in Chile. The setting is welcoming and breathtaking. Our Chilean friend bought 6 bottles of wine, so you know it's good. Next time, I'll try the bike tour too. One final thought: it's nice to patronize family owned and operated businesses, but it is even better when you learn that it's a really nice family. Rosemary, we can't thank you enough for this wonderful review, it really made our entire team's day. Thank you so much for taking the time to come to visit again and we're so glad that this visit improved on the last and that your wine knowledgeable friend enjoyed our wines as well. Beth sends her greetings and we're all looking forward to having you back next time for a bike tour around the vineyards. Thank you so much for your support of our family business.

review_text: We shopped around on Main Street for a tour operator that could take us up. Everyone was very kind and some still had place. The climb to the mountain is highly weather dependent so ask aorund for the best day to go! We had a clear day with lots of sun in late spring we went up with some 200 people! The climb up is definitely a challenge and you need a good hiking condition. But we had a kind guide that was very encouraging and took plenty of small breaks and some larger to rest and enjoy the view. From the rim of the vulcano you feel amazing realizing that you made it! After some great picture moments and a break with amazing views with vulcano all around and a beautiful view of vulcano Osorno to the south. Getting down felt like a challenging when looking down at the steep slopes. Donning the gear provided by the tour operator and receiving instruction on how to use your ice axe to break we sat down in the frist toboggan slide to make our way down. Seeing others in front of us drop down the ledge made it only more scary. But once we got going it was exhilarating and so much fun. Sliding down this great mountain on small sleds in several small portions laughing and whooping.

review_text: We were in San Pedro between the days 27/12 and 03/01. The overall evaluation was positive. We made 8 tours in 6 days. All the tours were contracted in Brazil, with Leila. When we got there we had no downtime. Everything went as planned. All guides and drivers educated and prepared. Excellent transportation vans! We started with puritama thermas (in this tour we did not have roupão, as other agencies offer, but did not miss) and ended with the volcano. All thought for our acclimatization. I felt security and responsibility on the part of the agency. The ride to the Rainbow Valley was excellent, breakfast very good, Flavian guide great!! O passeio ao Vale de la Luna tbm mt bom. Maybe, the most beautiful and imposing, after the vulcao.The guide Cristopher is wonderful and the driver Reinaldo exceptional. They offered a very good snack, with drinks of wine and sour pisco at will. The geyser ride, the salary route and red stones were beautiful! The rise to the Lascar volcano was amazing. We got to the edge of the crater and gave to look inside. The guide Francisca left us peaceful and passed us a lot of safety and confidence. She took us in a wonderful truck! A breakfast was served before climbing the volcano and then a snack during the climb. We finished the tour after 17:00, could have offered another snack, after all, were 12 hours of tour in total. But I would like to make two constructive comments. One about the Astronomical Tour: there was much to be desired. Maybe our expectations were too high. We imagined seeing the sky better than we saw. Maybe the city light was a little disturbed, because the place was close to the city. We had great expectations, pq say that the sky of atacama is the cleanest and clearest in the world. And the photographer could direct the scene, saying which pose is better, pq we only have 2 chances. And as I expected, my photo wasn’t the same as Instagram. I suggest that the photographer direct the scene and have patience at this very special moment for us tourists. Remember that there are only 2 chances for 2 photos (one chance for photo cads). We can't see how the picture was. 5 working days after they send us the photos. The other is about lunch at the end of the Ruta de Salares tour. We were offered a lunch at a restaurant upon arrival from San Pedro, at 3 p.m. The lunch was rice, chicken with cooked carrots and zucchini, crude lime and cabbage; mango juice; lemon mousse. I speak for me and for Leo, but the group consisting of other Brazilians tbm commented with us that they did not like. Our reasons are: 1) the food was without spice; 2) this is a type of food that we eat in Brazil, on a daily basis; 3) could have served something from local cuisine that, though simple, would have its value; 4) if the same food had been served in a village it would have a different meaning; 5) I would rather not have lunch and have the opportunity to eat something delicious in the city, even an empanada. 6) lunch could have been served earlier. The Jadrec guide is perfect: very funny and cult. I recommend Leila and Alabalti. Olá! Muito obrigado por compartilhar sua experiência detalhada com a Alabalti Atacama! 🌟 Ficamos muito felizes em saber que sua viagem foi incrível e que conseguimos proporcionar passeios inesquecíveis. É gratificante saber que desde o primeiro contato com a Leila, ainda no Brasil, até a realização dos 8 passeios, tudo correu conforme o planejado, garantindo segurança, conforto e organização. Agradecemos também pelos elogios à nossa equipe de guias e motoristas, como Flaviano, Cristopher, Francisca e Jadrec, além do excepcional trabalho do Reinaldo, que se dedicam a tornar cada experiência no Deserto do Atacama única e especial. Sobre suas sugestões construtivas, agradecemos muito! O Tour Astronômico realmente é uma das experiências mais aguardadas, e entendemos que a expectativa pode ser alta. Levaremos em consideração seu feedback sobre a iluminação e o direcionamento para as fotos, pois nosso objetivo é sempre oferecer a melhor experiência possível. Quanto ao almoço na Ruta dos Salares, sentimos muito que não tenha atendido às suas expectativas. Estamos sempre buscando formas de aprimorar nossos serviços e oferecer opções que proporcionem uma experiência gastronômica mais alinhada com a cultura local e com as preferências dos nossos viajantes. Seu feedback é extremamente valioso, pois nos ajuda a melhorar e continuar oferecendo um serviço de excelência. Agradecemos muito pela recomendação e esperamos recebê-los novamente para novas aventuras inesquecíveis no Deserto do Atacama! 🚐🏜️✨ Um grande abraço da equipe Alabalti Atacama! 💛

review_text: We rented a bike in San Pedro for 6000 CHLP/person/6 hours and rode to Laguna Cejar. review_text: I've really slacked on my reviews of places and activities but when one like this comes around, it's really the least I could do. Cooking classes with Boris were the best choice we made during our whole trip to Chile. My husband and I were there June 2013 and were very lucky to get Boris for ourselves for our experience. He was so professional and so friendly. The food was amazing yes, but what made the class was just hanging out with Boris. We started at 4pm and it went into the night. The whole experience, from going to the market and picking out the ingredients (he doesn't keep anything in the cooking studio but salt basically) so everything was fresh! I am hispanic and although I asked for us to speak in Spanish for my husband to practice, his English is excellent! Once the ingredients were bought, we headed back to the studio. It's a great space, lots of light, counter space, dining area, and right in front of where we were staying, The Yellow House (also, great place to stay!). He put some great music on and we did whatever he said to do! You can tell he loves to be in the kitchen, he gives very clear instructions of what to do but isn't bossy at all. He enjoys showing people but is not always hovering over your shoulder only doing things his way. I have taken several cooking classes and I find that the chef's way of directing students makes or breaks the class. He is very supportive and made us laugh all the way through. The Pisco Sour was the best we'd had (I thought I hated them until I tried what he made). We had wine and sat down for our 4 course meal: Avocado with fish sausages (the Fish terrine with avocado carpaccio), 3 kinds of Empanadas with Pebre (salsa), Pastel de choclo and Drunken Pears for dessert with Mote con Huesillo just so we could try it. He sent us an email attachment with all the recipes (plus others) so no need to write things down! We ate and drank until we were a happy, tipsy and very full bunch. It was such a good time, we left after midnight! I could've stayed there all day but we had to leave Valparaiso the next morning. Bottom line: I cannot recommend this place enough! If you are in Valparaiso, you have to sign up for a class. It was worth every penny!! You will remember it with a smile for the rest of your trip :)

review_text: I generally shy away from writing negative reviews of attractions, and usually ignore most when I view the TripAdvisor site. This one, however, is one I wish I would have paid more attention to prior to my visit. The vineyard is about a half hour outside of the downtown area, through some neighborhoods, and finally to the estate. There is a security gate that you have to pass, and reservations are required to tour (though we were able to make them same day). Tours were offered in English and Spanish, though most of my group spoke Spanish and the guide answered some of the questions posed in Spanish back in Spanish. Once parked, you have to visit the ticket booth to pay for the tour, then head to the waiting area on the grounds. The "Traditional" tour itself was about an hour, and included three main stops and three wine tastings. The first two wines were around $10 per bottle for the US market, and the final was around the $50 price point. The stops themselves, were fairly uninteresting. The first stop was at the Concha Toro house, but just the grounds outside. We were able to hang around what is now primarily office space and admire the few sculptures in the garden. No one is permitted to enter the house/office area. We then walked back to view the 20 different varieties of grapes that are grown by the company at the different facilities they own, though most grown at this location are Cabernet. When grapes have sprouted, they claim to let you taste them, but we were far too early in the year for buds. The next stop was for a white wine tasting, which included a glass for use with our red wine tastings later. We then went into the cellar house, where they had barrels out, though they admitted they were empty. We went into the Devil's Cellar for a brief movie type presentation shown on either end of the wall, and then to the original bottle storage room. Finally, we went to the red wine tasting station and had two pours, in the same glass as our white wine was poured. The vineyard did not provide any water to rinse glasses between tastings (the glasses are to keep). Finally, the group was able to exit through the gift shop. Knowing now how the tour was going to progress, we probably would have skipped this and done something else with our vacation time. There is a plaza that has wifi access at the end of the tour, but the connection itself was rather slow (my guess is that a lot of people were on it). Bottom line - the wine was nothing extraordinary, and the tour was a fluff piece for the brands they sell, for somewhere around $12,000 pesos per person (October 2015).

review_text: This was our second two week trip arranged by Liz in a two year period. The prior trip was to Chile, this one was to Argentina and Uruguay. It was another fabulous experience--she is every bit as knowledgeable about Argentina and Uruguay (and other countries) as about Chile. Everything was completely worth the cost--no way could we have done this on our own. Her guides especially are impressive--I don't know how she finds them--each of the 4 who helped us on this trip were charming, friendly, spoke flawless English, and were expert in their fields as well history, art, and politics-- by the end of our time we felt each were friends. For example, Cali, our guide in Uruguay, owns an organic farm and operates a farm to table restaurant with her husband; Mariele, our guide for wineries in Mendoza, works for a British wine magazine and is the daughter of an art professor. Everything was perfectly planned, down to accomodating our food and hotel design preferences and my husband's mild disability; she remembered all of our trivial quirks from the prior trip. Just one example: somehow she was able to arrange a private one on one winery tour and tasting for us with 80 year old Pedro Rosell of Bodega Cruzat--the charming, award winning rock star of South American sparkling wine. Liz truly makes you feel like a pampered celebrity--she is the absolute best. Highly recommended!

review_text: Leo Cruzmar is not just a tour guide…he is the consummate host. Making a connection with him via email was easy before our trip and then he connected with us via phone once in Santiago. Punctual, polite, knowledgeable, humorous… everything a good host should be. We spent half a day with him enjoying the sights and sounds of Santiago…from residential areas to the city we got a great feel for its peoples, architectures, and parks. The next day we spent with Rodrigo on an interesting trip to the port of Valparaiso, about 1.5 hours away from Santiago. Again, like Leo, Rodrigo displayed the same mannerisms and kept us entertained on the drive with his vast knowledge of the areas we passed through to Valparaiso. We walked through Valparaiso enjoying the hustle and bustle of the wharfs and city and made our way up the hill to a broad vista over city and the Pacific coastline. On our return we stopped at the beautiful Casas de Bosque Vineyard and had an excellent lunch. We highly recommend Leo and Rodrigo at Private Tours Chile for an in-depth experience of Santiago and its surrounds.

review_text: How to begin....after spending 4 days in Buenos Aires, a day in Colonia, Uruguay, and 2 days in Vina/Valpo....our best experience was the 3 plus hours we spent with Rodolfo of La Bicicleta Verde. We had only been in town 4 hours before our night tour began and we were immediately infected with the love and wonder our guide has for this beautiful place and its people. We are fit 50 year olds and the pacing and the stops were perfect. It was a treat to meet company owner Peter later and hear his take on this great city. We had to leave for home the next day so we were unable to spend more time with these guys but we are already investigating how to amass more frequent flier miles to get back to Chile and La Bicicleta Verde. (The bikes are sturdy which is good because some of the side streets are cobble so we think that kind of bike is the right choice for this flat tour area.)

review_text: Destilería Pisco Mistral is a wonderful place to visit for a day trip. The drive in from La Serena is beautiful, as is the distillery itself. Our group speaks some Spanish, but we booked an English tour in advance by emailing contacto@destileriapiscomistral.cl (this is listed on the Spanish version of their website). I received a prompt email confirming our booking for a 3:30pm English tour. We were able to park in a large dirt parking lot just past the distillery, for 1,000 CLP per hour. We paid for our tour in the gift shop area (6,000 CLP per person) and were guided around the distillery by Sofia. The tour was fairly short, but interesting, and Sofia did a great job of answering questions. The tour ended with a tasting of two piscos (you get to keep your glass); you also get a free drink at the bar, the pisco sour is delicious. The atmosphere of the distillery is gorgeous, as there are cobblestones, trellises, and greenery and flowers everywhere. Our group purchased several bottles of pisco as gifts; the prices at the distillery are definitely better than a grocery store we checked in La Serena. You can also get a personalized bottle that you fill yourself if you like. Up the street there is a small market selling jewelry, magnets, and other small souvenirs. If you have time, stop at El Cobre in Vicuna (on the way from La Serena) for delicious ice cream. Overall, this was a lovely way to spend a day!

review_text: This 9.5-hour day trip (not including time to/from the hotel) from Santiago was the perfect thing for us 2 days before our cruise leaves from San Antonio. Turistik has a very efficient operation using several smaller buses to collect people from hotels all over and bring everyone to a central meeting place to transfer to a large comfortable bus for the tour. The tour included everything advertised plus a quick wine tasting stop. Rest stops we’re well timed. Valparaíso is a fascinating place, despite the decades long decay of some structures and heavy graffiti from the Oct-Dec 2019 protests. A 1.5 hour stroll through brightly colored neighborhoods (virtually all of it downhill) provided a close/up view and understanding of the city’s development. Neighboring Viña Del Mar, which is newer and in quite good shape compliments Valparaiso. The recommended restaurant has high quality and plentiful fresh food at a reasonable price. Our guide, Eduardo, snapped several pictures of people on the tour throughout the day and emailed them to each individual upon request. This was a very nice added touch. Eduardo is a pro. He provided excellent commentary in both English and Spanish and had detailed answers for every question. I’m very glad we did this tour! review_text: Yes, Nevados de Chillan is is a pain in the butt to get to. Stay at the area or in nearby Las Trancas. Be prepared to deal with Chilean time which is like Hawaii time for y'all from the U.S. This is a great resort for these reasons: 1. Huge ski area with a lot of terrain for all skill levels. Groomed runs (on piste) are wide and great to bomb down. 2. Off-piste and out of bounds opens up endless terrain. Endless. Bonus: most of the skiers and snowboarders here are beginners, so you can always get fresh tracks, all day going out side country/OB. Pro Tip: make your way to the Refugio Garganta del Diablo. 3. Cat-skiing option is relatively inexpensive and opens up even more, wide open terrain. You get taken to the top saddle between the two volcanoes--Volcan Chillan nuevo and viejo. Also it is guided, duh, and a ski patroler also accompanies your group. BTW - our guide was AWESOME. 4. Restaurant Pillan: mid-mountain beers with sweeping, gorgeous views? Yes, please. This area sucks because: 1. Lifts, although beautiful, are old and slow, and there are not enough of them opening up the mountain. I don't mind that there are so few. I like having side country to myself, but they're excruciatingly slow. They have the two longest and slowest two seaters in the world. 2. I've heard about upper mountain closures due to weather. Luckily, we never experienced this. I imagine only getting to ride the one chair at tree level sucks. Ew. Really, that's all I have for you. This is a killer area that I hope to enjoy again in the future.

review_text: My husband and I took the Navimag ferry from Puerto Montt to Puerto Natales a couple of years ago with friends and we all absolutely loved the experience. As everyone else has said, this is not a luxury cruise but is comfortable enough and provides a unique experience to sail through the stunning chilean fjords with lots of interesting nature and beauty along the way! Including glaciers, remote islands and lots of wildlife! Perhaps we were lucky but we saw lots of dolphins, whales and birds along the way which was very exciting indeed, especially when the captain would spot them and call us to see them! We found the food to be simple but plentiful and tasty - no complaints there. The bar area was great too. We chose a 4 person sharing private room which was very comfortable and the shared bathrooms were clean. If you'd like some more detailed information and see lots of photos from our trip, have a look at our article at: http://worldlynomads.com/index.php/sailing-the-chilean-fjords-with-navimag-ferry/ Overall we'd really recommend this experience, especially as a wonderful alternative to lots of long bus journeys south from Puerto Montt to Puerto Natales! It was truly an unexpected highlight to our Chilean adventure.

Lucas, his associate also did a great job insuring our safety. In the afternoon we did the Parks and Politics tour with Hector and Lucas. Once again Hector was full of knowledge and information. We learned so much about Chile and its history from him. He really was great. The morning tour was in Spanish and the afternoon one was in English. Therefore, I can attest to the fact that his language fluency in both languages is equally good. I highly recommend these tours as a great way to see Santiago! review_text: I confess that I was afraid to catch huge queues for everything and lack of infrastructure according to some reports and videos I saw on social networks in July and August. I went for business to Chile and we decided to meet Valle Nevado and to our surprise it was simply amazing! We didn't get in line for absolutely nothing, we bought the tickets online the day before the visit, we went with our own car and it was a very enjoyable ride! There was no queue to exchange the ticket for the ticket, there was no queue for clothes, nor for equipment and restaurants. It was simply wonderful and everything very well organized. Bathrooms were even clean because of the low number of people circulating. There was room to sit in every restaurant, even in the outdoor areas. Yes, the road to the Valley is somewhat dangerous, from a bit of fear, if you are afraid go with an operator, but the rest can do everything on your own. We bought the ski day with class and it was great, I was able to learn and go down the Newbie pistes (not to be mistaken, has steep curves and descents yes) The secret is to go off season.

review_text: We closed all our tours with this company and, after the experiences we had, I felt obligated to alert those who are considering doing the same. During the ride to Piedras Rojas in May 2025, we experienced an extremely worrying situation: the driver simply stopped the car in the middle of the road to throw water in the face because he couldn’t stay awake. Yes, you read right. He was so sleepy that he had to stop to try to stay awake — putting the lives of all passengers at risk. This is completely unacceptable. In addition, we note a lack of preparation and organization on the part of the agency. On the same tour, the guide did not know how to handle a difficult passenger: an American tourist decided to shop during a stop to the bathroom, delaying the whole group. Because of this, some subsequent stops were shortened to make up for lost time, which undermined our experience. Another very negative point was the after-sales of the tours to Bolivia. Here is an important warning: when you close the tour with this agency (or with other Brazilian agencies), they actually outsource the service to a Bolivian agency. In our case, the return to Atacama was terrible. The car that brought us back was unhealthy. The trip lasted about 3 hours and the seats were so tight that my husband (which measures 1.76m) could not bend his knees and had to travel sitting on his side. We reported the situation to Thiago (representative of the agency), and the only response we received was: “Talk to the driver.” That is, you hire the agency and then try to get everything right, because the support simply doesn't exist. Other negative points that deserve attention: • Lack of communication from drivers: on some tours, the driver did not inform the search order of the passengers or where they were, unlike other more organized professionals we had. • Incorrect information about the tours: During a conversation with my husband, Thiago said that floating in the Baltinache Lagunas would be done in a clear-water lagoon (which led us to choose this tour instead of the Laguna Cejar). However, that wasn’t true — the lagoon where we floated didn’t have clear water, which was disappointing. In short, consider these points before you close your tours. Counting with other agencies I saw that the difference between them is little. Sometimes paying a little more expensive and having a better service than saving 50 reais and risking life.

review_text: We went on three tours with Whipala (based on Trip Advisor reviews): Tatio Geysers, Valley of the Moon and Red Rocks. All were good but the Valley of the Moon was the most crowded of the three tour destinations. Tatio Geysers The Tatio Geysers tour included an unexpected "safari", which was a delightful surprise on our way back to San Pedro as our guide pointed out vigunas (wild llama-like animals), zorros rojos (red foxes), llamas, wild donkeys, vizcacha (rabbits) and a multitude of water birds including tagua (giant coot) and pato puna (a blue-billed duck). Such touches helped offset the disappointment of not being at the geysers at dawn. The bus was about 30 mins late leaving San Pedro so we didn't arrive at the geysers until well after dawn. While this was an irritation for my husband who wanted to capture the first rays of light penetrating the steam, the geysers were a stunning sight. The rest of the tour went without a hitch and the guide led the group to the least busy areas so we could enjoy the peace and beauty of the landscape. The thermal bath was empty of all but our group, so the half dozen folk who went in had plenty of space. Breakfast was a simple but tasty array of ham, cheese, avocado and scrambled egg eaten on local bread rolls. Tea and Nescafe was available to wash it all down. (Note to those who like British style tea, Chileans generally don't add cold milk to black tea. You will be offered coffee creamer on the Whipala tour. In cafes you will have to explain you want "te caliente con leche frio" but even then you may struggle to be understood.) Our guide spoke excellent English and demonstrated a deep knowledge of the area and its geology. The temperature is low (-12 or so) and it can be windy. Dress for the snow to get the best of the experience (other day tours require the same level of clothing). Valley of the Moon This is an afternoon tour that can be done on the same day as the Tatio Geysers. The walk from the car park isn't long but the ground is uneven and sandy in places (I regretted not taking my hiking stick). The lookout is next to large sand dunes and close to a gypsum encrusted red stone landscape. It is an eerie and odd juxtaposition that is worth the effort. A short drive away we were able to walk through the gypsum coated land before jumping back in the coach to get to the sunset viewpoint. This is a photographer's landscape but timing is everything, so serious snappers should travel independently. Red Rocks This full day tour to the high country is worth the travel time since the landscape is stunning. Our guide was informative and fun. The Red Rocks are next to a frozen lake and the colours are sublime. It was windy when we went but thermal layers topped by a waterproof jacket, face covering and gloves were just about right to deal with the cold. The lagoons we visited afterwards weren't quite as fiercely cold. We saw vigunas and a red fox during the drive. The included lunch was simple and adequate but nothing to get excited about.

The landscape is absolutely stunning and unique and I would immediately go on this tour again.

review_text: Ko'Kayak was recommended to two friends and me by the hostel we were staying at in Puerto Varas, and we ended up going on two trips with Ko'Kayak: 1) rafting the Petrohué river and 2) sea kayaking the bottom of the Petrohué river into a fjord near Cochamó. Both trips were excellent. The rafting trip was a good way to spend an afternoon, with knowledgeable guides, good equipment, and nice views of the nearby scenery. The portion of the river that we rafted was Class III, and the water was cool, fast, and fun. The two-day sea kayaking trip was probably the highlight of my entire three weeks that I spent in Chile and Argentina. We began where we disembarked from the rafting trip the day earlier, where the waters of the Petrohué grew calm. Our guide, Niccolo, prepared the two double kayaks for my friends and me (I shared a kayak with Niccolo since this was my first sea kayaking experience). After a few hours of kayaking down the Petrohué, we stopped for the first meal along the riverbank (all meals were included and quite good). The afternoon brought us to the small and refreshing Ralún Hot Springs before we entered the fjord and kayaked to our camp for the night: a small farm along the fjord where the owners prepared an excellent dinner for us and a hearty breakfast in the morning. (We camped in a tent we brought, but Ko'Kayak provides tents.) In the morning, we continued paddling out into the fjord past Cochamó. We stopped for a relaxing lunch and then continued back towards Cochamó to meet the pick-up van. Throughout the entire sea kayaking trip, we couldn't have asked for better weather, and the views over the two days were spectacular. Niccolo spoke excellent English, and he was a great guide in tune with his surroundings. Review of: Rafting rio Petrohue Hey Andrew Thanks for your great review. We also had great fun paddling around with you guys. Hope your french trip is going well. Say hello from us all to Tiff and Greg. Kind regards. Richard Carrier

review_text: We have been skiing in Chile and Argentina every winter (summer in the USA) for the past 10 years. We have been to every major ski resort and with out a doubt Valle Nevado is the best ski resort in South America. Skiing in South America is very iffy. Some years there is no snow at all, often there may be only a couple of large dumps a season. Valle Nevado seems to have the most reliable snow conditions due to its high altitude, and its snow making facilities. They do an excellent job of grooming the trails with what snow they have. They generally groom the trails too well, plowing down any mogals that might have formed. Off piste can be very good, but often times the snow conditions are not very good off piste towards the end of the season, usless you are lucky enough to be there right after a dump. They have a very good lift system, and the trails are well layed out. I do wish they would replace the T bars in the back with chair lifts, rather than wasting their money by putting in a useless Gondola servicing the lower mountain parking lot. Valle Nevado is interconnected with its two neighboring resorts, so it is possible to ski to all of them from the Hotels at Valle Nevado. This year they had two free lift tickets to its neighbors if you stay 7 days. In the past you had to buy a separate reduced price ticket to ski at its neighbors. I can't say any thing about the rental equipment because we always bring our own gear with us, and we have never taken lesson there, but I have heard good things about the instructors in general. The resorts in the USA and Europe are much larger, have better lift systems, and much more reliable snow, and great instructors , but if you want to ski in July, August and September the only choice other than Glacier skiing, is South America (or New Zealand). Thank you Boston Skier for your positive comments about Valle Nevado. The resort does in fact, as you state, have the best snow in South America on average, both in quality and quantity. Please come and visit us this year as we open two new lifts and new terrain. As you state, Valle Nevado has access to La Parva and El Colorado and these three resorts together measure 7,000 acres. That makes the Three Valleys the second-largest ski resort in the Americas! We invite you to come back this 2013 and see what we have in store for you, including a new terrain park, gondola, and a day visitor service area with parking, lockers, ticket office and rentals.

review_text: We booked the 'Alyan Sunset Experience' during our 10-day trip through Chile. Even though the website said they only offered tours in Spanish & Portuguese (we speak neither), we booked it anyway because 'gustamos el vino!' We soon learned the owners (ALycia y ANdres = 'Alyan'), one of their daughters, and our guide (Rose) spoke fantastic English and made us feel incredibly welcome. Even though there were a couple hundred people there for the experience, they broke us up into smaller language-specific groups and it felt much more intimate than being herded like cattle through the property. We've been on plenty of winery tours, but Rose surprised us with how many little tidbits of information we've never heard before. She shared the origins of 'Sauvignon' grapes ('Savage' in French) typically grew wild and the glacial minerals and dry climate in the Maipo region perfectly stress the vines so they produce the right amount of tannins and flavor. We also learned the Carmenere grapes were thought to be wiped out due to a fungus outbreak in Europe until they discovered what was called a 'Chilean Merlot' was actually the only remaining Carmenere grapes in the world; and Chile happens to be where they grow the best. Another knowledge nugget was that roses are planted at either end of the rows of grapevines because they serve as a warning sign of potential bug infestation, since the same invasive bugs who love to eat grapevines also love to eat roses. Long-story, short: Rose was chock full of knowledge and one of the best and most knowledgeable guides we've ever met! We thought the quality of the wines were some of the best we found in Chile and we particularly enjoyed their unique and delicious Carmenere. During our initial orientation, Andres shared his philosophical perspectives and why he is so passionate about wine. Thank you for your nice words and for taking time to leave a comment. We are very happy to know you enjoyed the day here in Aysén. review_text: We were picked up by Frank and Jose and spent the next three days with them on a private tour. Now that we are at the end of our trip to Chile, visiting the Atacama is my favourite compared to Easter Island and Santiago and area, not only due to the beautiful scenery but also because of our guide and driver. They were always punctual during morning pickups, courteous, great with our kids, had answers for our questions, and gave us plenty of time at each location. They were happy to stop and let us take pictures from the roadside when we spotted donkeys, vicuñas, etc. On our last day, after El Taito, instead of heading back to San Pedro where we would have 30min for lunch before driving to Calama, we asked to go directly to Calama, which they accommodated. We went through some amazing scenery with hardly anyone else in sight, and had enough time to have a nice lunch together in Calama before they dropped us off at the airport. Dear, Thank you very much for sharing the experience, we are very proud that you have enjoyed our service, because it makes us improve every day, we invite you to continue living new experiences in the other regions where we operate. A warm greeting from the entire TurisTour team.

review_text: The hotel is set in the beautiful foothills of Torres Del Paine National Park. There is a spa, bar and two restaurants. The food is creative and pretty good. The customer service is also good for any needs. The rooms and bathrooms were clean but could use an upgrade. We booked a full day Paine tour (9:30a-8pm)which included the Glacier Grey cruise. Roads in the park are all gravel and rough and can be treacherous. Our tour guide Julianna was incredibly friendly and informative (English speaker). She and driver Sebastian took us to Must See sights all morning and we stopped at several photo ops. Don't let the words "boxed lunch" fool you into thinking it was a sub par lunch. We stopped at a scenic picnic area and were served huge sandwiches with sides, then out came the platters of meats, cheeses, nuts, pastries, soft drinks and wine. After the cruise we stopped on the way home again to more incredible views, information and food/drinks. Worth the hefty price. The day was long but never dragged.

review_text: The tour was definitely worth the money. Our guide was knowledeable and genuinely seemed to enjoy himself while working. He took some great photos which are shared via whatsapp. The time spent in the city of Valparaiso is sufficient and we had an excellent lunch. However, I do not believe visiting the fish district is a necessary stop and it is obvious why other tour companies do not stop there either. If you have been to one fish district, you have been to them all. There simply isn't much to do unless you are brave enough to eat some fresh ceviche. And there is a very good chance that you will be crapped on by the hundreds of seagulls anxiously awaiting their next meal. The time wasted on the fish district brings me to my next criticism, which is how little time is spent at Viña del Mar. The vineyard is beautiful, but it it is basically a pit stop. You are rushed into the wine tasting area where you are given 3 different glasses of wine and then you have a little free time before heading home. My advice is to skip the fish district and spend more time at the vineyard. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago

review_text: We went on the 3D2N tour, one way from San Pedro de Atacama to Uyuni. We had struggled for a long time to find a tour company we were happy with, after reading terrible reviews and horror stories online. But as soon as we went into Cruz Andina's office we felt welcomed and well informed about the tour. We had read great reviews about Mijael (Magic Mike) and luckily he was running a tour on the day we wanted to go! The tour was great and we were very happy with our decision. There was a group of 9 of us so there were 2 cars. Both cars were in great condition and the drivers were checking the tyre pressures and engines etc during the tour, which made us feel very safe. Mike was a wonderful driver, never going too fast and always checking we felt okay on the roads. His English is amazing and he is so knowledgeable about the area, you can tell he really likes his job. The hostels we stayed in were better than expected, some of the group were in dorm rooms but my boyfriend and I were given a private room both nights. The first hostel was cold but there were hot showers, and the second night in the salt hotel was warmer and is lovely and in a beautiful location. The food is very nice, but I would recommend bringing some of your own snacks too. On the last day at the salt flats, both Mike and the other driver were great at the perspective shots. They knew exactly what to do and helped us with whatever we wanted. When the tour had ended Mike even gave us a lift to our hostel in Uyuni, which he didn't have to do. I was quite nervous about going on the tour beforehand, but I would highly recommend it now. We felt safe and looked after and enjoyed the whole thing. Thanks for everything Mike!

review_text: They saved our stay in San Pedro During our trip to San Pedro de Atacama, the Mitampi agency was key to making our experience incredible. We had originally booked our tours with another agency, but due to bad weather they started canceling them without warning, which complicated our planning quite a bit. Fortunately, Mitampi helped us sort everything out quickly and make the most of our stay. They were super committed, even managing to include us in tours that were already full, looking for all possible options so that we did not lose any experience. Mauro, the driver of the van, was excellent: very good vibes, played perfect music for each trip, and also the food they offered on tours was exquisite. As for the guides, the best was Juan, who could be seen to have deeply managed the knowledge of the area and conveyed it clearly and enthusiastically. We also had Ignacio (we think it's called that), who was only partially handling the information, and that tour was a bit rushed. Finally, Luis, unfortunately knew almost nothing of the place, although we understand that that is not necessarily the responsibility of the agency. The astronomical tour was a great experience. Diego, the photographer, was very friendly, professional and patient. If a photo didn’t go well, he would gladly take the time to repeat it. As for Franco, who was guiding astronomical observation, we think he could improve his treatment somewhat: sometimes his responses to errors were somewhat harsh, and it would be better if he could transform those errors into learning opportunities, without dismotivating. As for the vendors, Juan and Jero were very friendly from day one. They guided us patiently, resolved our doubts and helped us put together the entire journey. On prices, if you take more than one tour they make discounts, especially if you pay in cash, which allows you to access more convenient rates. The quality of the tours was excellent. In short, a very committed, close, flexible and recommended agency. Thank you very much, Mitampi, for all your support and willingness!

review_text: This is the best exhibition of pre-colonial Chile and south America south of Mexico City. Housed in a old building around two courtyards, it is excellently laid-out with magnificent artefacts, most of which are pottery or stone, but do look also at the metals and wonderful textiles. Above all see the quipu exhibition (this was the "abacus" which was like a sring to tie round your waist, with coloured and knotted strings hanging down from it, the original indigenous people used it to reckon up the taxes owed and report back to the chiefs). There is an excellent shop on the ground floor, which has the best collection of books and music of the Mapuche and other indigenous people I know of locally. A great experience both for tourists and experts.

review_text: So, my wife and I are ardent Napa/Sonoma "wine snobs" and had only been exposed to cheap Chilean wines here in the US...and mostly because "the good stuff" is hard to get in California. So it was with a little trepidation when our Chilean friend suggested we tour Santa Rita winery. WE LOVED IT! Now, I'm not going to sugar coat this review and say that their entry level wines are all that good...but their premium wines certainly can hold their own against any Napa/Bordeaux wines in the same class. I'm now scouring our local wine spots here to find their high end wines. We had an absolutely wonderful time with our tour leader Catalina who lead the English speaking tour for us. She was very knowledgeable about the history of Chilean wines, how the wine manufacturing process works, and the chilling story of how this winery played a pivotal role in Chile's history. All the staff there was very friendly and we had a great time hanging out in their winery store drinking glasses of their top wines and chatting with the store manager. We got to see their very impressive bottling plant and you'll be blown away at how efficient their processes are. The grounds are immaculate and it was overall a great experience! Highly recommend! Thank you very much for your congratulations! It is very gratifying to know that you enjoyed your experience at Viña Santa Rita and we would love to welcome you again.

So it was with a little trepidation when our Chilean friend suggested we tour Santa Rita winery. WE LOVED IT! Now, I'm not going to sugar coat this review and say that their entry level wines are all that good...but their premium wines certainly can hold their own against any Napa/Bordeaux wines in the same class. I'm now scouring our local wine spots here to find their high end wines. We had an absolutely wonderful time with our tour leader Catalina who lead the English speaking tour for us. She was very knowledgeable about the history of Chilean wines, how the wine manufacturing process works, and the chilling story of how this winery played a pivotal role in Chile's history. All the staff there was very friendly and we had a great time hanging out in their winery store drinking glasses of their top wines and chatting with the store manager. We got to see their very impressive bottling plant and you'll be blown away at how efficient their processes are. The grounds are immaculate and it was overall a great experience! Highly recommend! Thank you very much for your congratulations! It is very gratifying to know that you enjoyed your experience at Viña Santa Rita and we would love to welcome you again.

review_text: We booked a package of four tours over three days, very helpful over email when trying to arrange the tours and get information on the different tours available, and very quick responses. We did the Valle de la Luna, Atacama Salt Flats, Cejar Lagoon and the Geysers. You visit the office to pay for the tours before your first tour and they give you a list of timings, where you'll be collected from and what to wear/bring on each tour. The cost of the tours does not include entry fees so you pay these whilst on the tour. The number of the people on the tours were quite small which was good and they try to get to the most 'touristy' places before the other big tour groups. All the guides speak English very well, and the tour is given in English and Spanish. Some of their guides were really excellent and had so much passion for the desert, it's history and geology. However one guide we had for two of our tours did not show this level of enthusiasm and his role only really seemed to transport us between places and prepare our breakfast/snacks. I would recommend booking tours with Whipala, it was very smooth and we enjoyed all the tours we went on.

There are at least two other toilets in the park. Good place to cycle round. There are a couple of walking paths and these are a little hard going if it's very hot, do take water with you. These paths are completely optional. The mixture of sand, rocks (in many different colours) and salt are breathtaking.

review_text: Buy a half day tour (Rather costly) in Santiago, as the bodega is located more than an hours travel by metro-bus and taxi. If you do not speak spanish it is a little complicated to get there. If you do so, be aware that you will have to cross one of the most risky areas south of Santiago. You will have to pay entrance fee to get in. Includes 3 tastings. See their website. The tour of the bodega takes less than half an hour, and you will see no production on the tour. If you have been visiting other wine yards and bodegas in Chile or Argentina, no news will be added concerning fabrication of wine. But the complex is nice, and the wine shop will sell their wine to the same price as you pay in the shops in Santiago. But you will get a free wine glass as a souvenir. We went on to Mendoza, and took a full day bike tour visiting several bodegas in the Maipu area and found it much more fun. In all bodegas we heard the same story about producing wine, and in all places you will have to pay for the tour and to taste their products.

review_text: The name of the hill was given by Pedro de Valdivia in 1541. It is believed that an Inca settlement existed at this site when he arrived, with kings and authorities as happened in Cuzco. It was something of a provincial capital with an Inca administrative and ceremonial center. So rather than founding a city Pedro de Valdivia only took possession of it. Between 1814 and 1817 two forts or castles were built: Hidalgo Castle (originally called Battery Santa Lucia) on the site where it is currently located and Castillo González, on the site that today occupies the Caupolican Terrace. The transformation of the hill into a beautiful urban public walk begins only between 1872 and 1874 with the construction of ponds, water fountains, terraces prepared for vegetation, carriage paths, gardens, the hermitage of the Virgin of the Hill and viewpoints following the French landscape design of the time. Open from Tuesday to Sunday from 9 am to 8 pm in summer and from 9 am to 6 pm in winter. Free admission. At the entrance that is at the intersection of Merced and St. Lucia Streets is a Fountain of Neptune with his wife Amphitrite: It is smaller than the one on the other entrance to the hill, on Av. From the Liberator Bernardo de O’Higgins (La Alameda) The sites visited are: Hidalgo Castle, the Caupolican Terrace with the Spanish Gate and the Caupolican Sculpture, the Vicuña Mackenna hermitage, Pedro de Valdivia Square and the terrace and Fountain of Neptune at the exit of the hill in the Alameda.

review_text: What a truly exceptional experience...demanding exercise, history lessons, beautiful countryside, delicious food, and incredible people. Who could ask for anything more. When I first booked the tour online I was a little concerned that Andres would be out of the country and unable to accompany us, but he assured me that he had arranged for an exceptional guide and assistant...and he did. My sister and I enjoyed every moment of our time with Carola and Gabriel. They took turns riding along with us and driving the support vehicle so we could always go at our pace. Carola's knowledge was seemingly endless and she was willing to speak to us in Spanish to help us practice until the topic got too complex or we got too tired and then she seamlessly shifted to English. I would not have made it to Farrellones without the Gabriel riding along with me, providing encouragement without ever pushing. On the Andes to Ocean tour, our cycling included one day of gentle riding through neighborhoods, government districts and parks within the City of Santiago, a grueling day climbing the 40 curves (switchbacks) on the road to Farrellones, a day of gentle rolling hills in the white wine country of Casablanca Valley, and a day of up and down winding roads of Leyda Valley. Our guides were incredibly attentive and willing to modify anything and everything to suit out interests and desires -- modifying food and drink selections each day based on our preferences, taking us on shopping excursions, etc. They made picnic lunches seem elegant, and the homemade food prepared by one of the daughters of Andres and Ines was outstanding -- absolutely the best spinach pie I have ever had! The cycling was great but only part of the overall experience. When we walked the streets of Valparaiso and ate a barbecue dinner and shopped for traditional clay pottery in Pomaire, it felt as if we were spending time with friends, not just guides. I would highly recommend Paseos en Bicicleta and I hope to return someday soon to join them for another tour...this time to Patagonia!

review_text: After a lot of research, we closed all our tours with Atacama Magic and we have nothing to regret. They were incredible experiences. I can't help but thank the attendants Micéias and Alice. Before, during and after the tours they always helped us with everything. Even due to weather reasons, some tours had to be rescheduled and they do everything they can to fit the tour into another date compatible with your period in the city. They are very helpful and polite. They provide security for tourists. We took the astronomical tour with guide Lasse, a German who lives in Atacama. Although the moon was already hindering the visibility of the stars, his presentation was engaging and captivating. We stayed around the tenth reflecting pool as he immersed us in the story of the stars from a Greek and Andean point of view. Fantastic! We took the tours of Laguna Cejar, Geiser Tatio and Valle de la Luna with the guide Rodrigo. Good people, funny as hell and knowledgeable about each place. The tours were excellent and at the end a pisco snack was served. They were very good. Highlight for the Valle de la Luna tour whose driver was Dario, a nice Bolivian who was willing to be our photographer during the sunset that day. Nice guy who loves Brazil. A hug for him. We did the best “good” tour, which is Piedras Rojas with the guide Marta Argel. It was a show! He explained Chile's political division to the differences between the region's camelids. Take a tablet with you and immerse the tourist while we're on the way. When you arrive, you already have an idea of everything and can just enjoy the landscape. It was fantastic. That day, we were driven by the driver Weimar, who made sure no one was left behind and was quick to serve breakfast and lunch. We also did the Salar de Uyuni with the agency. Our guide was excellent, comfortable car, plentiful food (you don't even need to take food, seriously). It's an unmissable tour. The best outside the region. But the best tour in the region was the climb to Láscar. It was challenging and rewarding. Unique experience. We booked with Atacama Magic too, although I believe they delegate the tour to nortrek. It was too crazy. Do it. They're already there. Just be aware that, as it is a less popular tour, it is common for the day that was scheduled to be canceled due to lack of tourists. So line it up correctly. Our guide Krusty did everything to make you psychologically prepared for the mountain and we won. Do not fool yourself. When you arrive at the base you get a shake hahaha And that. Thank you very much Atacama Magic! 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻

review_text: If you want the opportunity to experience the amazing scenery and environment in this fabulous place, this tour company should be avoided at all costs. When booking tours be careful to make sure that the tour group is small, and that you will have opportunities to experience the environment rather than looking at the scenery from inside a bus!

review_text: We have just arrived in Uyuni after the 3 day 2 night tour from San Pedro De Atacama. Having a great group was largely luck of the draw but everything was well organised, food was generally good and accommodation, although basic, was perfectly pleasant. The salt hostel lost electricity for a few hours on our second night but these things are sometimes inevitable in the middle of nowhere! The jeep ride can be bumpy but our driver Nelson was fantastic and very safe. The only little negative is that there were no seat belts in the back but as you are on dirt roads with little or no other traffic it felt very safe. Some of our group suffered with altitude sickness so be prepared if you are not used to the altitude as the tour reaches almost 5000 meters. This tour will definitely be one of the highlights of my trip to South America. Needless to say the sights are simply stunning and quite literally take your breath away, and for those who are used to hostels and budget travelling I think you will be pleasantly surprised by the food and accommodation. We also took the Valley de la Luna and El Tatio Geyser tours with World White and were highly impressed. Whilst guides on these tours spoke good English, the Uyuni guide didn't but we had a Spanish and English speaker in our group who could translate. If you don't speak Spanish I recommend asking the tour companies who else is booked on the tour to see if there are Spanish speakers who can help you. Allegedly you can pay 30,000 pesos more for an English speaking guide but this seems quite pricy to me and for us just didn't seem worth it. Tips wise I would suggest taking more than the 200 bolivianos they suggest as there are markets and places to buy wine etc and the 200 only just covers park entrance fees. Also almost everywhere charges for the toilet. Remember toilet paper, bottled water and snacks. They provide ample food but sometimes snacks are just necessary!

review_text: The stars in the middle of the Atacama are beautiful. We went during the lunar eclipse, which made the stars even brighter. However, the telescopes are terrible - old and outdated. You could buy a better telescope easily, or a friend probably already has one. Not worth the money to go out and use the equipment. If you can find a bus to drive you to a secluded spot in the desert and wait for you for several hours, that would be more worth your money. On the positive side, the guides were incredibly nice and knew a ton. They engaged well with the audience and they were very good at describing cosmic motion in a way that could be understood by the layperson. If you speak Spanish, which luckily I do. In summary, if you know nothing about stars/constellations/the moon and you speak Spanish fluently, go on the tour to learn. If you know nothing but don't speak Spanish, find a dark corner of the Atacama alone. If you already know the basics, don't bother with the observatory.

review_text: Went for a day trip to Valle Nevado, Farellones and El Colorado ski areas in the Andes. Enotours picked us up at 815 am and drove us to a central meeting point for our tour. Our guide was Patricio Bello and Driver Helmut. True gentlemen and comfortable ride. Before entering the road to the Andes, our guide made a stop for people who needed a bit more warm clothing and boots. The store rents the items for the day with a short stop upon our return to return the rented items. The temperature was in the high 30's F so my wife and I were comfortable with jeans, gym shoes, a light sweater and light jacket. 2 lane highway thru the Andes to the summit of Farellones Ski Area, our first stop. Please if you get car sick take Dramamine as there are 40 hairpin turns to the summit. It is a safe road and was a safe trip plus the driver stopped going up 2 times for acclimation to altitude and photo ops. A stop included the Valley of the Condors en route up the mountains. Condors were seen flying above us. No problems. The next stop was Valle Nevado Ski Area to rest and use facilities plus get a coffee at the Hotel and a bit more picture taking. Great views, good service in the hotel. Back to the van to our final stop of Farellones for lunch (not included) and wine tasting, much wine tasting. A great chance to meet your fellow travelers. There were 5 on the tour including 2 Americans, 2 Brasilians and a Mexican. All became instant friends over lunch. Lunch was great, service by staff was excellent. Down the mountain we go with a number of stops for photo opportunity and a little rest. Again Entour came thru with a delightful, beautiful and exciting day. Thanks to Patricio and Helmut for a safe, secure and informative trip. Muchas gracias mi amigos. Skiing and wine-tasting are the two best ways to experience Chile! We're happy you visited us for a day, we hope you make the trip here again and stay with us so that you can experience our warm hospitality.

review_text: I didn't want to leave this place, and neither will you. What a gem. My family and I visited Kingston on the second day of our two week trip in Chile, Argentina, and Uruguay. It was my favorite thing about the entire two weeks. Don't be taken back by the lack of signage and the slight confusion of the entrance to the vineyard - be happy that you are going to a winery that is not overrun by hordes of tourists getting off of giant buses and people just popping in off the roads because the saw the sign. All tours must be pre-booked in advanced, and you are guaranteed to be treated like you are the most special person to ever set foot there. We were lucky to be greeted by Andy, the husband of Courtney Kingston. He gave us - myself and my parents - a private tour. We were also lucky to bet here during harvest season, so some of the staff were hard at work sorting the grapes. It was fun to see the process in action. I learned so much from Andy, and you could feel the passion that he and his family has for wine, Chile, and their land. We had our first tastings in a beautiful seating area that they have overlooking the vineyards. Following our tour and tasting, we had lunch on site at their outdoor "restaurant." A wonderful lunch of three courses - salad, fish, and dessert, with each paired smartly with one of their wines. I loved each and every wine we tasted. The food was delicious, and perfect for on warm, sunny day of wine tasting. Our service during lunch was also wonderful. This was the only winery we visited in Chile and Mendoza, Argentina in which I purchased wine. I ordered a whole case of Syrah that is going to be shipped in two days and I cannot wait. My mom asked Andy if they did weddings. He said they have had only one before. If I ever get married, I would totally consider Kingston as a location - it had that much of an effect on me. Kingston Family Vineyards, you completely won me over! I cannot wait to come back in the future, and I look forward to ordering more wines! Abby, it was great hosting you and your parents for your lunch with us at Kingston Family, and thank you for the kind words. And yes, if you ever want to stay longer for an even more momentous event, we'll be glad to host you for it :-) Thank you again for visiting us, and we look forward to hopefully seeing you again...

review_text: Chris was a phenomenal guide and we had the best experience on this tour! Everyone was so friendly, supportive, and caring. review_text: I was researching a guidebook with my family. We had been to various springs along the Carretera Austral but this one takes the biscuit. There are multiple pools at increasing temperatures, including very hot. The settig is idyllic, blending in with the surroundings so you feel you are part of the forest and fjord. Some pools are like infinity pools in hotels, where you can gaze out over the fjord and trees. Truly a marvellous setting. There are more luxury all inclusive hot spring resorts with accomodation along the Carretera that are also amazing; or more isolated springs that are an adventure to get to... but for an accessible day-trip spa this sets the standard. The kids loved it, there is a decent (and reasonably priced) restaurant, and this stretch of the original Carretera is a great region to visit, with Cochamo and the Hualaihue peninsular so close. Highly recommended, and I've been to almost all of them!

review_text: Today’s Bike Tour Adventure in Santiago Today we had an amazing bike ride with a fantastic tour guide named Alejandra. She was incredibly friendly and full of expert knowledge, guiding us effortlessly through the vibrant streets of Santiago. The meeting point was just a short walk from our hotel, making it super convenient to begin the adventure. Alejandra led us first to a beautiful sculpture park, where we got to enjoy open spaces and unique art installations. From there, we rode down into the lively markets, weaving through charming cobbled streets nestled at the foot of San Cristóbal Hill. We parked our bikes and strolled through the bustling market, taking in the sights, sounds, and scents of local life. Alejandra treated us to freshly made juice—strawberry and blueberry—which was as refreshing as it was delicious. After exploring the markets, we sat down to enjoy a traditional Chilean snack called a sopapito, served with a flavourful chili sauce that was absolutely delicious. We eventually made our way back to the meeting point, feeling enriched and uplifted. It was a perfect way to experience the local culture, explore a slice of the city, and have so much fun doing it. Review of: Santiago Markets Small Group Bike Tour

review_text: I had a wonderful day on this tour. It is very well paced with more than enough time to chat and experience each area but, full of interesting places and things to see. I was picked up from my hotel on time by Rodrigo, our driver, and we were on our way after collecting Helen, our guide, and a few more people. About halfway to the coast we had a short stop to try some local Chilean snacks and then off to Viña del Mar to see a Moaï statue, the coast and the Flower clock. Then, a short drive to Valparaiso where Helen took us on a walking tour around one of the colourful neighbourhoods and shared her love of Chile with us. A photographers dream with so many subjects to point your lens at. After a lovely lunch in a location with a view to die for, we set off back to Santiago via Viña Indómita for some wine tasting and a view over the beautiful valley. We were each dropped off at our hotels at the end of a lovely day. Helen is great and full of knowledge about Chile and the areas we visited. She is bilingual, Spanish & English, and chatted to us with ease. A really lovely person. Rodrigo drove us around with such competence through all the traffic, down narrow lanes and up steep roads without breaking a sweat. He is a very good driver. review_text: After finishing the "W" in Torres del Paine, we were picked up by out Leslie and Luis and began the next leg of our Patagonian adventure. We were outfitted with the highest quality of gear and afterwards, we began our instruction into river kayaking. We were a group of 5 friends, athletic, but not much kayaking experience. However for the next 3 days, we were in the company of experts with Leslie, Luis, and Christian. Kayaking between icebergs, beside glaciers, through beautiful rivers, and next to panoramic views of the park, we were in awe of the surroundings. We were continually surprised at the things they pulled out of kayaks: french press coffee, sandwiches, and chocolates. At camp, they pulled out all the stops with gourmet food and skills-- which was easily the best food of our trip. In addition to the excellent amenities and gorgeous views, we found ourselves in great company with our new friends. I highly recommend Kayak en Patagonia for those looking for a true Patagonian river adventure.

review_text: Note - This is a review of the SAT8 overnight tour. We were collected by Jorge mid afternoon and driven around 40 minutes out into the Atacama desert where a small camp was readily prepared. We arrived to welcome drinks and nibbles which we enjoyed whisky getting to know Jorge before a fantastic meal was prepared by Jorge's wife Joanna. A couple of hours after sunset we wrapped up warm (blankets and hot drinks provided!) and started an engaging 90 minute astronomy class from Jorge which was tailored to our knowledge level. His passion for the night sky was evident throughout the lesson and he was able to answer all of our questions. It's worth noting that by this time the sky looks wonderful with the milky way appearing clear and bright even to the human eye. After the lesson we had unlimited time to observe planets, stars and other galaxies using the advanced telescopes Jorge brings along. His photography knowledge was also really helpful as he assisted in taking magical shots with both his and our camera. Overall, delicious food, great camping and astronomy equipment and we learnt much more than we ever expected. Needless to say this tour doesn't come cheap however just ask yourself if you'll ever get a chance to do anything like this in your life again. Highly recommended!

The visit is quite short as it is essentially just looking through around 8 rooms of his house which are spread out across the hillside location - but it was nevertheless fascinating. The only access is via a guided tour, and it seems we may have been lucky to have only had to wait for half an hour for tickets. It may be worth booking in advance

review_text: Last Saturday, May 31st we visited Viña Terranoble in Fundo Santa Camila, San Clemente, Maule Region, our visit was without prior scheduling, bearing in mind the above consideration, we were received in an extraordinary way by our hostess who gave us a personalized tour of the vineyard facilities. With deep knowledge and great enthusiasm, Carla Echeverria, our hostess, told us about the history, growth and types of wine production of the vineyard. We tasted two of their iconic Carmenere wines, Azara and Civis, it was simply spectacular. Personally I found the inspiration and creativity behind the names of their wines very interesting, reflecting the history, essence and spirit of the vineyard. Of note is the winemaker Marcelo García’s ability to create and inspire. It is advisable to make the view early, tour the premises and enjoy a tasting will take at least 2 hours. The values of their wines are according to their quality, I recommend tasting the Azara line in all its varieties. The cost of the tour is affordable and certainly satisfies wine lovers. The journey from Talca to the vineyard is an expeditious route and in very good condition. There are ideal locations to leave photographic records. Highlighting the attention and treatment offered by our hostess, was very friendly and friendly with an excellent willingness to answer our inquiries regarding the characteristics and properties of the wines, definitely made us feel at home. His passion for what he does is contagious and allowed us to live an indelible experience. In short, our visit to Viña Terranoble was perfect, recommended for an afternoon with family or friends.-

review_text: This museum holds the objects found in some of the surrounding attractions. They have objects like shells, bones and arrowheads from Pichasca National Monument, and they also have some of the rock art from the Enchanted Valley National Monument (Valle del Encanto). Although it would have been nice to leave SOME objects at Pichasca, this museum is invaluable in telling the story of the history of the Limari valley, and of the migration of the people's in Chile and particularly in this region. Wonderfully kept, with interesting pieces such as mummies from the Altiplano, and a Moai from Easter Island. What the museum does not say however, is that the Moai was once left neglected by the side of the road in La Serena until it was covered in graffiti. They cleaned it up and sent it on a world tour, where it was accidentally beheaded! The insurance money paid for the restoration and the room it is now in. You can barely see the joins at the neck - unless you look real close. All the information is in Spanish, so as usual, not really for English speakers - but the Spanish is a little easier than the usual Chilean information boards found elsewhere. It is a cheap entrance fee, and is also free on Sundays - so go then if possible.

Novice riders need not fret, as the trail is just challenging enough and the horses dependable. review_text: This was a nice, peaceful & scenic way to get from Puerto Montt to Puerto Natales. We had a twin cabin to ourselves which was a decent size. The only problem being at the front is the first two nights you here and feel the crashing of the waves as the boat tackles the 1m to 5m waves. The on board doctor gives sea sickness tablets to nearly everyone. There are three things which spoilt the trip which means we wouldn’t do it again and now realise the money is better spent in the Torres Del Paine. 1) The food was worse than I remember school dinners being. The “hot” main courses were all luke warm. The veg was always cold. Pudding was jelly one night, then an awful attempt at rice pudding (I do like rice pudding) and semolina. From our room we could see the staff canteen which was nicely laid out and they had lovely food. Considering the price we paid I think the staff were having a laugh with the food budgets, making sure they did ok. 2) They said we would arrive in Puerto Natales at 11am on the Monday. They are quick to announce everything else (where we are on the journey to look out for things on other days), but on Monday there were a clear lack of announcements. Word then went round we would not get there to 6pm. This then caused everyone to ask the staff individually which they didn’t seem to like (JUST MAKE AN ANNOUNCEMENT!). One previously nice guy, curtly said “Idon’t know, ask my manager”. Once in Puerto Natales it then took us 2.5 hours to dock. This appeared to be because NaviMag can’t be bothered to pay for tugs to help us dock. When we did get a tug it didn’t take long. They put it down to the high winds (which are always there). 3) Once we docked at 7pm. There was then one announcement saying dinner was served. What?!?? We are 8 hours late docking, we are now docked why are we now told dinner is served? All the staff do a disappearing act again. review_text: We booked several tours with Amulen-Ko, talking through each of them with Roberto and Sofi. The TV setup they have is a great way to preview the adventures you’re interested in. Both canyon tours, and their volcano tour, were excellent. Coni and Gabriel (canyon tours) were super knowledgeable about the region, the activities, and the town if you need any recommendations (we checked out several of their recs in and around Pucón and were extremely happy with the results). They were great conversationalists, so much so that you almost (keyword almost) forget you’re about to rope down a 90 meter waterfall. It was our first time canyoning and thanks to their safety guidance and welcoming personalities, it won’t be our last. Edgar practically lives on the volcano. I love when my guides play where they work - it really shows in their knowledge of the land, and tips and tricks they’ve picked up themselves along the way. We got the luck of the draw and had Edgar to ourselves (we were the only people who signed up for that day), and he became part tour guide, part personal photographer as he took some stunning photos and videos of our time on the mountain. Even just the three of us, there was never a lull in conversation (his English is excellent) or camaraderie; from learning how to properly forecast the weather for a mountain, to conversations about our lives, the day sledding down the volcano with Edgar was a core memory of our time in Pucon, and our entire trip in South America. Every time we’ve walked in town since the treks, we still stop by to say hi to whoever is hanging around the office - they’re just a welcoming staff all around. Did I mention they somehow have some of the best pricing in town?

In the end, we had to miss the lake district entirely which was terribly disappointing. But we are so grateful to Andres for making alternative plans for our family, including a last-minute hotel reservation in another town and private transfer from the airport at 2:30am! review_text: There are lots of review about the trip to Salar de Uyuni itself, so this review will just focus on the company we went with, Lithium Aventura. They did lots right at the start. Our driver was slow and careful, the food was good, and our accommodation was basic but exactly what was promised. We saw some stunning scenery. Things started to go wrong on the second day, when the drivers in our group (3 cars) told us the town of Uyuni was blockaded and if we went there we would not be able to get out. They offered to drive us to a nearby town for usd$50 pp...considering the whole three day trip including food, accommodation and driver was USD$140, this price was extortionate. Especially given, the last day of the actual tour was not completed, and instead the last day was cut in half in order to get to Challapata in the hope of finding onwards transport. The thing that really made us angry was that our driver let slip they'd known about the blockade for the last FIVE days...ie before we'd set out on the tour. Lithium hadn't bothered to tell us this, or to arrange for us to be dropped off in a different town. Instead, they just left us to try and work something out with the drivers. Eventually, we agreed to go with them at a price of USD$43 pp (still extortionate for a pretty short drive). Our driver promised us there were lots of buses in the town he was dropping us off in. He promised he'd get us on one; of course, he didn't. He took off once he had the money. We were left on the side of the road in Challapata at 4.30pm. There was one bus available with standing room only for 3.5 hours. We got on, but it was obviously pretty crap after getting up at 5.30am, and after my girlfriend had been sick due to the altitude. We arrived in Potosi at close to 9pm with no accommodation. Basically, these guys scammed us and we couldn't recommend them because they were so dishonest. The icing on the cake was when we realised the driver pushing for $50pp was from a company with awful reviews who Lithium had specifically promised they refused to work with.

I didn't book a return to the airport and when I tried to book online, with several attempts, the site would not accept my payment so I had to give up and take a taxi. So when I returned to Santiago, I booked a return this time. The trip to my accommodation (a different place) was fine but when I was outside waiting for my minibus on my departure one went right past just after the appointed time although I was jumping up and down and waving. I don't know if it was the one meant for me or not. I tried phoning but all the 'press buttons' are too much in a foreign language and it cost me a lot and I didn't even speak to anyone. I emailed them but by the time someone phoned me and said a bus was on the way, I had panicked and taken a taxi as I couldn't be sure that Transvip would turn up. Either the one that went past or one that was late was for me - or they forgot and just sent one after they got my email. I have said all this to them and think i should have got a refund on my return fare but my request has been ignored. It cost me a lot more than that as I had the phone call and the taxi. So, fine from the airport but don't risk a return!

review_text: We booked a half day winery and bicycle tour. It takes around 40 minutes to travel there from Santiago (but that was on a weekend without the mid-week traffic chaos of peak hours in Santiago). Out tour included a 9km bicycle tour taking in both the Carmen and Santa Rita vineyards, a tour and explanation of thew wine making process at the Carmen winery, and then wine tasting back at Santa Rita. We had two excellent guides (Carolina and Juan Pablo) who explained the details of the wine production and of the different wines that we were tasting and how best to appreciate them. The cycle tour was fun, all on the flat and relatively easy at any reasonable level of fitness and on a sunny day it was a really pleasant way to get some moderate exercise. The tour of the wine making rooms at the Carmen winery and the tasting at Santa Rita were both also highlights.
