review_text: We have done a 9 day tour of Chile with Chile-on-the-go organized by Catalina. We have started in the Laker District where we toured national parks and the volcano Osorno for 2 days, then we flew to Patagonia. We stayed in Punta Arenas overnight taking a boat ride to see the Magellan penguin colony on the Magdalena island and the sea lion colony on the Marta island. After that we took a bus to Puerto Natales where we visited the Torres del Paine National Park and explore fiords with wild life. Then we flew to Santiago and Valparaiso where we toured the cities and surrounding Andes. The tour was unbelievable. It was perfectly organized. We were picked up by local drivers always on time. The country is so beautiful, especially Patagonia. Catalina has done an outstanding job! It was definitely worth the money!! Seva and Anna Polotsky

review_text: This was a really really fine day in Santiago. Thanks a lot to City Trekking Guide and especially to my guide Alicia. She adapted the tour perfectly to my wishes and interests and showed me a lot of nice, remarkable and impressing places, for example a quiet and beautiful park (Parque Forestal), the Rio Mapocho with an interesting mural painting, the Plaza de Armas with the cathedral, La Moneda and two lively markets. We had a very good lunch in the Mercado Central. According to my wish we also visited the Cementerio General where I could see and learn very much about the history of Chile, about immigration and social classes. The cementery is a green oasis in the city. Very touching was the visit of the monument for the victims of the dictatorship. Alicia told and explained me a lot about the city, about the history and the present of Santiago and Chile. She did this in a very friendly, lively and competent way, so I enjoyed every minute of the tour. She also gave me information about activities which I wanted to do on my own, for example a visit to the Museo de la Memoria (which I would highly recommend). Before I came to Santiago somebody had told me that this city would not have much to offer to the visitor. After the tour with Alicia and City Trekking Guide I know that this is nonsense. I would have liked to stay longer and to have more time for this city and country. Dear Lothar Schmidt, Thank you for your words. I am glad that you have liked so much the tour with our guide Alicia that you would like stay longer!! She tried to customized the experience for you and i know that she has been more than happy to have met you and show you around Santiago, Valparaíso and the mountains. We will be waiting for you here. There is still too many places to see!! On behalf of our team, i wish you the best in your future =) Keep in touch! Regards, Ignacio

review_text: Full day hike which can be pretty long and challenging at times. We did it in 8 hours of actual hiking time, plus 1 hour lunch break at the top. Three distinct parts: The first third climbs through scrub land. Takes a while to warm up and get into your stride. Nice view at "windy pass". El Chileno refuge is a good place to take a first decent break. The second third is within a forested environment. Trees provided some welcome shade on the hot day we were there. Less climbing and flatter in this section of the hike. Very much the bit we enjoyed the most. The last third is the most challenging. You come out of the forested bit and climb up and across a glacial moraine in order to get to the top. The moraine bit is quite challenging. Large rocks and boulders, can get pretty steep. It's also the last part of the hike and you are pretty tired by the time you hit this hardest bit. BUT, all worthwhile in the end when you get to the top: amazing views of the towers, surrounding mountains, and glacial lagoon.

Because it was off season we went for one that was 5000 pesos instead of the normal 7000. The boat ride is only 30 minutes but given there are not many Penguins in March it is long enough. All of the info was in Spanish so we didn't get much out of that but seeing a penguin was cool. After we went for a walk along a dirt road to get some lovely views of the cliffs. All round a great day out!

review_text: After my first successful Santiago/Valpo trip, I booked Hector again for a longer stay. Admittedly I'm a bit OCD, and thankfully Hector was thorough and prompt with our MANY emails back & forth. He arranged everything from transfers, to a flat in Providencia, to wine tastings. Pick up's were always prompt, in his great Mercedes minivan. The flat was a 2BR apartment in a highrise, clean, with a good view of downtown Stgo, very well located, within a few blocks from restaurants and the metro. Hector is a wine lover like us, and he expertly arranged our tastings over 3 days, and a fantastic walking tour in Valpo. Highlights of our tastings included Antiyal (a must-visit organic & biodynamic boutique winery) and Kingston (Pinot is fantastic). Trust Hector when it comes to food as well. He chose a great restaurant for lunch on the edge of a hill with a nice view, as well as the best damn sandwich local joint ever, Lomit's. Hector treated us like old friends, very easy going, organized, and fun to hang out with! Great job, again!!

review_text: Definitely worth the early morning wake up to drive up to the geysers and watch the sun come up over the Andes Mountains (over the Bolivian side). The geysers are quite spectacular and the amount of steam contrasts against the cold morning air. The area where the geysers are is well maintained. You can only walk on the paths marked out for your own safety. Arriving 30 mins or so before sunrise is plenty of time to walk around and then watch the sun come up. Its very, very cold before sunrise - lots of layers and thermals under trousers. I wore a fleece, a hoody and a down jackets and I was still cold pre-sunrise. Wool hats and gloves are a must! Also, the altitude can bother some people. Take it slow and drink lots water before you arrive.

review_text: I spent more time here than what I had planned. It was incredibly educational, and I learned so much about modern Chilean history. I was vaguely familiar with Pinochet, but did not learn much about him or the history of Chile in school (even though the dictatorship was within my lifetime). This museum more than compensated for my previous lack of education, and I would recommend the tour to anyone who wants to understand South American political history. The second floor of the museum (the floor right above the entrance) is depressing, to say the least. It was difficult to see all of the artifacts from such a violent and tragic time. But this is also what makes the museum so important from an educational standpoint. I will remember a lot more of the details than if I had simply read about it in a book. The third floor is much more uplifting in documenting the eventual restoration of democracy in Chile. In addition to historical video footage (displayed very well), the audio guide is very helpful (available in multiple languages), especially if you’re not thoroughly fluent in comprehending Spanish. Entrance to the museum is free, but there is a nominal fee for the audio handset. One thing that was a bit confusing was the layout of the sequence of displays. I got lost a couple of times trying to figure out where to go next, especially given that I was following along with the audio guide. I noticed a few other people who seemed lost as well. I did finally figure out the layout, and I didn’t mind revisiting some of the displays. If there is one place to make a point to visit in Santiago, this is the place. The intentionality in preserving documents and artifacts is so important to reduce the likelihood of something similar happening in the future (at least in Chile). It’s tempting to want to forget about this tragic time in history, but the preservation of this historical memory is part of an important strategy in advocating for human rights in Chile and around the world.

review_text: Watch out for the scamsters who stand close, but just out of sight, of the security guard who takes the registrations required to enter the park. They approach you with a sheaf of papers, which looks as if they are there to register you, but in fact want to tell you they have a relative (I suspect in every country of the world you may come from), in exile from Pinochet’s regime, have a small poem they wish to give you, that they are students, and that a small donation of CH$20,000 would be of great assistance to them, and mere petty cash for you. Either, give them a coin, which will make them go away (not very happy), or tell them that you gave yesterday. If the registration guard is closer to the path leading up to the entrance, they (the scamsters) tend to move into the smaller part of the park across the road. The park itself, once registered to go in, houses an old castle, which requires a lot of climbing to reach. However, the pathway is for the most part well shaded, and there are plenty of interesting sights (and shops of varying prices) along the way. Much of the climbing also requires the negotiation of step narrow steps, which should be considered if physically disabled in any way. The view from the top is somewhat spoilt by the surrounding skyscrapers, but you still feel a sense of achievement and wonderment at having, in a sense, scaled the castle tower. Equally exciting is, being there at twelve noon, when a cannon is fired to signal the occasion.

review_text: My wife, my grandchild and I rode the funicular down from the top of Cerro San Christobal in January 2017. To get to the top of the mountain we took the gondola cars at the terriferico in the Providencia neighborhood. The gondola cars had no waiting line and were modern and new. We got a great view of the city as we ascended up the mountain. We took the funicular down from the top of the mountain. It was a pleasant and reasonably priced ride. We stopped as we were going down because the cars coming up the funicular stopped at the station part way up for the metropolitan zoo. We only waited about 5 minutes when both cars (up and down) started up again and then, in the middle, the cars passed each other at the only place where there were 2 separate tracks. review_text: We sailed from Ushuaia to Punta Arenas, and booked this trip as a break between our two trekking trips. It worked out perfectly. It was a great way to rest up and relax before the next round of hiking adventures while still being able to take in the extraordinary scenery. The ship itself is very comfortable, with great sight lines from almost any deck, inside or out. Our cabin was roomy enough for our 4 nights, and the bed was incredibly comfortable. The floor to ceiling cabin window was wonderful, especially when I saw the whale breach! All of the staff were friendly and professional. It was obvious that safety, especially during excursions, was of utmost importance. I won't soon forget the "zodiac cha-cha-cha"! The food was very good, and the flowing wine, beer, and pisco sours were nice to enjoy while gazing out the windows or wandering the decks. Our weather wasn't always the best, so it was nice to have the hot tea ready whenever I needed it. The shore excursions were also well organized and fun. We got up close to several glaciers in the zodiacs, enjoyed some short scenic hikes, and managed to land on Cape Horn despite the rough seas. Hot chocolate was often waiting for us, either on shore or once back on the ship. We also enjoyed and learned quite a bit from the evening presentations about Tierra del Fuego, although they did vary in quality. My husband and I don't usually care for cruises, but this small, personal ship really met our needs. I would highly recommend it!

review_text: My Wife and I just completed the 4 Day Sea Kayaking trip through Pumalin Park with Richard as our guide. With it being somewhat off season we were lucky to be the only 2 on this trip. We had an amazing experience! We can not thank Richard enough for the great trip. We had 2 days of on and off rain which made it pretty cold at this time of the year but after that the sun came out and the remainder of the trip was warm. The rain didn't really change the experience too much besides somewhat restricted views and cold wetsuits in the mornings. The views were fantastic when the sky was clear and were still magical when the clouds hovered through the fjords. Both of the hotsprings were amazing and scenic and unique in their own way. The first hotspring was located on an island at a hotel/hostel where we happened to be the only guests. We had 2 hot spring pools to ourselves where we enjoyed Pisco Sours while watching the Sunset while it occasionally rained on us. We camped at the Cahuelmo Hotsprings on the 3rd night. These hotsprings are perfect for engineers as in order to control the temperature of the various pools the flow needs to be modified by blocking the channels with mud and rocks. The food Richard cooked was excellent. Much more fancy than we are used to on our backpacking trips. He even brought along some wine and beer. We saw many Sea Lions including curious ones which came by to check out the kayaks. The Sea Lion colony was impressive. We also saw a few dolphins while sitting at camp the 2nd night. We can really only come up with 2 complaints. The wetsuits were cold and wet in the mornings after the rain. There is nothing that can be done to change that. Thankfully Richard was able to make it Sunny for the last 2 days. The second complaint is one of the sleeping pads provided by Ko'Kayak would not stay inflated. Again we can not really complain about it because bringing your own sleeping pad was recommended and inflatable sleeping pads have the tendency to be unreliable. It definitely isn't the first sleeping pad we have had fail on us. If you are okay with camping in tents (on nights 2 and 3), this trip is definitely worth taking! Richard is an excellent, knowledgeable, and personable guide. There is nothing we would change about the trip (except the sleeping pad). What to bring in October- *Warm Clothes *Rain Gear *Bathing Suit *Waterproof camera (I wish I would have brought a go pro) *Sun Glasses *Hat *Towel

review_text: Booking a tour with HecTour was one of the best decisions we made for our trip to South America! We arranged our tour via email and prepaid with PayPal before we left for our trip. We were very eager to see the wine region of Casablanca and as I'm a sommelier, Hector arranged our tour to be led by Natalia who is also a sommelier and has worked in many of the wineries in the Casablanca Valley. She did an AMAZING job! Natalia met us in Valparaíso with a large sign with our name - very professional and easy to see in the sea of people! We toured Vina Del Mar and Valparaíso including a ride on an ascensor and walking around Cerro Alegre before heading to our wine tour of Casablanca Valley. Hector also called Natalia during this time and had her hand the phone to me to make sure I was having a good time and that everything was going well. Great service! Natalia arranged for us to have lunch at Viña Indómita which has a beautiful view of the Valley and delicious food! We visited three wineries that day - Viña Indómita, Emiliana, and Kingston - before we were dropped off at our hotel in Santiago. It was the PERFECT day! We felt so comfortable with Natalia and our driver Rodrigo and learned so much about Chile! I highly recommend HecTour!

When we visited the office to pay, we were asked if we had a car. We said yes, but confirmed that we didn't have to drive. The employee, who wasn't the astronomer, confirmed and told us to meet at the office at the designated time and a van would be waiting to bring us. Once we got there and met the astronomer, the driver started complaining to him in Spanish that our friends had forgotten that they were supposed to drive and blamed them. What the driver didn't know is that our new friend is a Spanish teacher and knew what he was saying, not a good move. After talking with the astronomer, we figured out that the company had called the hotel of a different couple on the tour and asked them to bring their car. They were out touring all day and had not stopped back at their hotel. You are paying for the transportation as part of this experience, it is absolutely unacceptable to make people pay and then ask them to provide their own ride up the mountain in the middle of the dark with their front-wheel drive vehicle. The astronomer refunded our friends the "transportation" portion of the tour fee, but did not refund them the full amount. The driver did not apologize and was rude. After the star gazing ended, our friends told us that on the drive up they realized one of their headlights was pointing sideways and we needed to fix it before departing so they could see the road. We wanted to take 10 minutes to figure it out by going through the car manual and opening up the hood, but the driver didn't want to wait for us. We asked him to please stay, but he took the rest of the tour guests and left. The astronomer ended up asking us to wait for him to close up the observatory and then guided us down the mountain while we followed behind his car. However it's true that you were not meant to come with your car, and refunding to you the transportation fee only was not a fair compensation actually... All this could have been avoided by having one extra permanent personnel at the office, but we are just two astronomers running our private observatory, and we just can't afford that (so far),,, Now the good news: such misunderstood will never happen again because from last month we have more automatic remote telescopes installed on site (operated from USA astronomers), hence private cars are not allowed anymore, under any circumstance, so problem solved ! Your kind words about the observations and about us astronomers make me feel that all in all you had a good stargazing experience, which is our only relief for that evening...

review_text: We took the reverse path from the glacier to the torres. This path seemed to be a little counter-current, was extraordinary and we saved the best for last. Much recommended. Day 1: We went to refugio paine grande by boat, arrived at noon, made our way to the glacier passing by Lago Grey, slept in Paine Grande and then continued our W to the East. Day 2: We started by making our way partly into the valley that leads to Britannico (heavy rain stopped us about half way), moving further to Refugio Los Cuernos, where we spent the night. We saw an avalanche go quietly (at first) down the glacier. Far away, and a wonderful view. Day 3: We had a "rest" day hiking "only" to Refugio Torre Norte outside the park that day. We only did this because Chileno was already fully booked two months in advance for early November (spring - not yet high season). If you can avoid the senseless hike outside the park then go straight to Chileno. Day 4: We made our way up to Chileno, then to the Torres. We made sure to be there quite early at the advice of one of the nice hosts in Torre Norte (she considered the forecast and seemed to read it well - she advised being at the towers before 11, we arrived there at 10.30 am, and - really - clouds started masking the towers at about 11.30 am). I expect this was also in part luck though. The sight of the torres is unforgettable. If you have them clouded one day, and can stay another day, for heaven's sake do so. Then we hiked back, enjoying a Patagonian beer in Chileno. The bus departs close to Torre Norte/Central. After years, we still dream of this experience. The W trail is amazing, has close to zero difficulty other than masses of water on a "bad" day. It is suitable for every fitness level, so long as you are aware that even just walking for 80+ km in 4 days with luggage is straining. Bring chocolate bars - you ll need them and they'll be horribly expensive in the Refugios. Don't mind the refugios if you're older than 20 - you'll get through it :) Food there can be booked in the evening even if you did not do so before. We often did this spontaneously. Food was alright. Forget weather forecasts, rain is common just for an hour or so a day at least. Very likely, you will have rain at least one of your days. Bring rain garments for this reason. Camping was not an option for us, and seeing the pouring rain in real life, we were glad we did not do it. You'll likely have no phone reception in the park (which was enjoyable). The distances are accurate as for the privately owned parts of the park, and completely off for the public parts. Expect your walks on the public property to be longer. I suspect civil servants documented them more based on airline, while staff of the private part might have done the walking. Best experience of our lives - we made a photo book, and look at it often.

review_text: We decided to book the 3 day one way tour to uyuni with flamingo tours because of the friendly and well-informed people in the office and because they were a little more pricey than the usual ones, which made us think they would be good. Unfortunately they made us a lot of promises they did not fulfill. Half of the park was closed because of the snow so Laguna Verde, Laguna Colorado and the geysers and thermen were not accessible. Instead of a discount we had to pay 20k Bolivianos extra (because of more distance driving to get into the park). Next morning we got picked up by an annoyed driver at 4am instead of the 5am the people in the office told us. Luckily we were already awake. Appearedly Flamingo tours had dumped us with an other way cheaper agency because we were the only ones that had booked with flamingo tours. The others had all paid more than 20k less than us and they were all doing the 2-way (4 day) tour! With this cheap agency breakfast consisted of only bread, we didn't get the promised sleeping bags and were really cold at night, the last day our driver had such a hangover in the morning he fell asleep behind the wheel drove his car off the road... So we had to take the wheel over from him! Anyway, I suggest you to inform yourselves really well before booking the Uyuni tour with Flamingo tours. Do know they just dump you with another agency if their reservation is not full. Uyuni is really beautiful though and we had a lot of fun :)

review_text: Excellent, superb, amazing, trip of a lifetime ... all of these words describe our adventure to Pichilemu…thanks to Oceanos! Pichilemu feels like an old surfer town that hasn’t quite hit tourism yet. It feels like you’ve struck gold once you’ve found it, a treasure. The people are about as authentic as it gets. They are warm, inviting, encouraging and simply beautiful human beings. The culture matches the people perfectly. We stayed here for 6 days, and it was the perfect amount of time. My goal for this trip was to learn how to surf for the first time. Not only did I learn how to surf, but I learned how to read the waves, appreciate the process and be one with the sea. Ismael is an excellent surfer and teacher. I have never met a man so in tune with living out his dream. It makes you search within, and wonder what your own unique genius is/ and how can I bring that into the world to make it a better place? He teaches with passion, motivation and tremendous patience. He is with you all the way, picking the right places, the right conditions and the right waves to give you the best surfing experience possible! Ismael is also one of the most joyful people I have ever met, his heart for humanity is contagious. It is his absolute JOY to give you the best possible experience, and it comes from such a genuine place in his heart. His joy in teaching you how to surf reminds me of the quote, "Everything is new when you see it again with someone." It is his joy to watch you experience surfing, the culture, the town, the people, etc. for the first time. The cultural tour was wonderful. We visited local wineries, saw how they made local pottery, salt and wheat. I loved these days because it showed me how beautiful the journey can be. It made me appreciate the process of everything. The food was delicious. We awoke every morning with a fresh spread of avocado toast, juices, coffee, eggs or granola to start our day. Picnics by the beach or local food for lunch... Barbecue at night or a freshly cooked meal in the kitchen accompanied with superb wine! I also can say I watched the most beautiful sunset of my life! All of it was perfect. Ismael was the ultimate tour guide! You felt like you were getting a fabulous tour with a local insider, without feeling like a tourist. I never knew how much I could love a place and people in such a short time of meeting them. I was left with a full heart of gratitude and a deeper sense of who I am. I cannot say enough good things about Oceanos, Ismael and Victoria. They made this trip, one of a lifetime. Thank you for everything! Maggie was and absolute delight to host you... Thank you so much for come all the way to pichilemu. I'm so honored to receive such a getting from you.... Thank you for ever. Aloha, Ismael Herreros

Thanks for writing, we aim to meet all the expectations of our guests and your opinions help. Guests who stay at Valle Nevado for a week receive two interconnect tickets to El Colorado and La Parva, otherwise it is indeed possible to buy an interconnect ticket to ski two resorts. But given the size of Valle Nevado, sticking to one resort per day is recommended. Like all South America resorts, we do have a several surface lifts, but the resort does have a high-speed quad and several chairs, and the most modern lift system in Chile. review_text: If I could give ilovechile Tours a rating higher than 5, I would! They exceeded "excellent". We were with Fran for 3 tours (2-1/2 days) - the city tour, the Volcanic Springs Route and the tour to Valparaiso and Vina Del Mar. All three of these were excellent tours and presented so much knowledge and information to my family of four. The surroundings were beautiful and we felt like we saw so much in such a short period of time. And these tours were well worth the price - the day trips lasted from 9 to approximately 7. Not only did we learn about the sights and history, but we learned so much about the Chilean culture - the people, the music, the food, and day to day life. Fran was such a joy - very upbeat and helpful - always looking out for us. She went out of her way to make sure we were comfortable and getting out of the tour what we wanted. Fran spent time in the USA and her English is impeccable. She gave us recommendations about dinners and things to do in the evenings. She shared information on how they had started this tour business. We were truly glad to work with such a nice, genuine person. When Fran left us at the airport, she offered to always be a resource to us should we need other information or advice about future trips to Chile. She stated it very well -- we now have a Chilean friend to reach out to. We feel the same way! We recommend that you book with ilovechile tours. You will be happy you did! Review of: Valparaiso Day Trip from Santiago - Private Tour for Small Groups

review_text: I wanted to make a special wedding proposal, and no clichés. So I decided to surprise my (now) fiancee. Before anything, I chose to do it in the Santa Rita vineyard, because it was a place that neither my fiancée nor I knew. I came to think of getting in touch with the vineyard administration to ask for help, but I preferred to be spontaneous. We reserve the site and I hammered on the idea of taking the private tour. It was very easy to use the vineyard site, well structured and with lots of information, including how to arrive using public transportation (seriously, choose public transportation! It's easy and secure). We arrived at the entrance of the vineyard and the plan was to go carting to the main house (which would start circulating in half an hour), however, in the entrance we met Cynthia Garcia, tourism coordinator from there. Cynthia saw us coming on foot and knowing that we'd still have to wait for the carriage, offered us a ride to the main house, it was super! We were talking about “The killers” and listening to ”Somebody Told Me”. I swear to God, it wasn't arranged. Arriving there, we made the payment of the tour easily. Soon the guide Danielle came to greet us. What a lovely person! Speaking a Portuguese almost without accent, we preferred to go with the Spanish ride to train the lenguage. We began the tour with some explanations about the grapes and the story of who the founder of the Vineyard was. When we entered the vineyards I had no doubt, I asked Danielle to take a picture of us. When she realized that I was about to make a wedding proposal she promptly started filming with her own cellphone. It was sensational! The vineyards, chilly, intimate climate, was perfect! After that, the ride which was already very cool, became something even more special. Danielle articulated several "extras" on our tour. It was very funny, because the video of my marriage proposal viralized in the vineyard. Everyone came to wish us happiness and blessings. Danielle got a carriage ride (exclusive) by the indoor gardens, after that Cynthia received us in the main house, where we were presented with a bottle of the Casa Real Wine, the premium wine from Santa Rita vineyard. Besides, they got us a table at the Doña Paula, the vineyard's restaurant. We forgot to make the reservation. What a lunch! All very delicious. We toasted with the sparkling wine of the house! It was an incredible experience. I just have to thank all of the vineyards, especially Cynthia and Danielle. We will always return to Santa Rita, since we truly feel blessed with all the affection we received. I just wondered, what would it be like if I had planned? It happened as it had to happen. For sure it's the best vineyard in Chile, not just the wines... but also for the people, who make there a special place!

review_text: As a wine-loving couple on year-long (budget) adventure, this was a highlight on our trip down south through Chile. After researching many vineyards in Chile, this was the best choice for price, tour, tasting, location, and accessibility. We stayed in the town of Talca and went to the bus terminal to catch a bus just 20 minutes to San Javier. There are bus stops along the main road in San Javier, next to Balduzzi. After the turn off from the main highway, get off at one of those stops and make your way to the vineyard (I suggest downloading the app Maps.me which is really helpful for navigating, and the vineyard is on there). You can also tell the bus driver where you're going and they should drop you off in front. Balduzzi does not require a reservation, and charges only 9,000 pesos per person (~$13 USD) for the tour and tasting. The tour was given by a really nice, knowledgeable man (I wish I remembered his name!), and was very informative. We saw most of the facilities; the main house, grapes, the barrel storage, the bottling process, lab, etc. All were accompanied with relevant, interesting information to the wine-making process. The tasting was delicious too, which included 2 red and 2 white generous pours. The staff was incredibly generous and gregarious. To return, we waited at one of the bus stop across the street from the winery and caught a bus back to Talca. In total, we spent around 3-4 hours on this adventure. Totally recommend it!!!

review_text: This is the "main" cave and is contained within a small "island" at the western end of the section of coastline (of Lago General Carrera) containing the Marble Caves of Chile. It is a beautiful attraction when seen during early morning in bright sunshine. The best way of seeing it is by small boat from Bahia Mansa (about 5 k out of Puerto Rio Tranquilo to the southwest). The cathedral is only a 5 minute boat trip away! The boats from here cost about $15/head for a one hour trip. The best way of visiting is to rent a kayak on returning to the jetty at about $20 per hour. 2 hours would be enough to see the cathedral and the best of the caves. For anyone in the area, it is a must-see. For many, it is the main reason for visiting this region. We are just under 70 and loved it!

review_text: An absolutely beautiful day out. The lagoons are stunning and the colours and geology at Piedras Rochas is amazing. Definitely worth a trip. Look out for wildlife and bird life along the way as well as amazing plants (we visited in spring which made it more spectacular). Each of the sites is community run and restricts visitor numbers to preserve the places. You need to buy a ticket beforehand (the website isn't the easiest to use) and then check in at various range stations. The rangers are really helpful and the sites are beautifully taken care of - the toilets are amazing, something other tourist destinations in other countries could certainly learn from!! The peace, tranquillity and amazing colours make these sites a delight. Review of: Piedras Rojas Salt Flats and Altiplanic Lagoons

review_text: I paid around 350.00 per person to do the El Principal Sunset Tour. Unfortunately, it was raining that day and it would not be possible to have the full experience we purchased. Everything would be fine, if it weren't for the winery's lack of preparation in welcoming tourists on rainy days. Umbrellas were not provided, the tour was quick, explained in a hurry. At the end of the tour we were taken to a part on the side of the store, like an open balcony, to taste the wines and enjoy the cheese and cold cuts boards that were included. That's when the disappointment came. We all stood in the cold, tasting the wines. We couldn't hear the explanations because of the sound of the rain. When they released the cold cuts, people literally fell over the table to eat. It was impossible to taste anything. I think that for the price we paid, they could have placed us in a more comfortable place, instead of leaving us in the cold, standing, tasting the 3 labels they offer.

review_text: We booked the self guided bike tour. My bike broke down at the far reaches of the vineyard as soon as I reached the first hill. Third gear was fine but as soon as I went into first gear, the chain slipped off and I C realized the teeth were bent inward. I tried to fix it but was unable to. There was tons of caked oil and dirt throughout the cassette and chain and it was obvious the bike hadn’t been cleaned or serviced in a long time. I had to walk back to the winery. I asked for a partial refund but the agent said he had sent me off “with a working bike and you brought me back a bike that needs to be fixed.” For a winery that wants to be of this caliber and is this expensive, customer service should be paramount. He essentially blamed me, saying that I broke his bike. We ate lunch at Tanino which had very good food but is quite expensive. The grounds and winery were beautiful, but there were a constant stream of tour buses and tours. We got the burrata and tortellini which are both pictured.

review_text: One of the three best days of fly fishing for trout in my life! I have fished fresh and salt water all over the world using all kinds of techniques and caught all kinds of fish. The day with my expert guide Benjamin Vial on a remote lake in Chile was truly a Zen-of-fly-fishing experience. To get to that lake we drove gravel roads through several ranches (estancias) opening and closing locked gates (Ben has the keys) and then walked over a few rolling hills to get to a breathtakingly beautiful blue lake. During our hike we passes ponds which Ben studied to determine which insects were at what stage of their life-cycles. He check out the lake and confirmed his decision to go with a particular, tiny nymph fly. Wow, was he right! We walked along the shore sight casting to cruising brown trout. They pounded my nymph all day and I caught and released so many that I stopped taking photos. Mid day we gave the trout a rest and had a wonderful lunch prepared by Ben’s wife presented by Ben on a red and white checkered tablecloth laid out on the grass and tiny white flowers. We told stories about our lives and the fish we caught and those that got away. I am so happy that I can now include my day with Ben as one of my favorite stories.

review_text: I used Turistour in San Pedro de Atacama on a few occasions. It is the last trip that I booked with them that really was a total rip off. We booked the night before and given it had rained 2 -3 days earlier where some roads had been closed, the company must have known that they could only take us to 2 and not 3 of the tour stops. review_text: To the many positive reviews others have written about this museum – the casual adult visitors with kids we saw during our visit seemed to really enjoy themselves – must be added that this is a tremendously important historical collection of steam locomotives. It includes examples of American, European, and Japanese, as well as Chilean–made, engines spanning nearly the entire lifespan of the technology. From one of the few surviving Rogers 4-6-0's that I know of, complete with inside-the-frame valve gear and air reservoir and in service 1896 – 1972(!), to a sleek 1953 Mitsubishi 4-8-2, the quality-to-quantity ratio of this small collection is huge. The Rogers engine is posed over an inspection pit, accessible by stairs, which makes it possible to visually inspect the internal valve gear; it's the only place I know of where it is possible to actually see this early technique dating from the birth of steam locomotion and obsolete in the U.S. long before this engine came to Chile. The star of the collection, though, is a narrow gauge articulated 0-8-0+0-6-0T combined rod/rack-and-pinion locomotive made in the UK by Kitson-Meyer. It is one of only three surviving examples (two in Chile, one in Argentina) from the original nine in service on the Trans-Andes RR between the two countries, 1910 – 1971. The displays were well-placarded, including service histories in English; data was in Spanish only but was fairly easy to translate, although "Cremallera," meaning rack-and-pinion drive on the Kitson-Meyer display placard, translates literally to "zipper" in English (which, when you think about it, describes the arrangement of "teeth" between the rails – also on display – perfectly). All in all we spent the better part of two hours touring this thoughtfully laid out, very important, and well-maintained outdoor museum, and we would have been there even longer had the Estacion not been closed for apparent renovations. (My husband, a rail enthusiast wrote this review.)

review_text: My husband has a walking problem and can't walk for a long time. Valparaiso is a very colorful city best appreciated by walking. After searching the Internet, I found a perfect one that caters to our need - a private tour, reasonably priced and with a great tour guide (based on previous reviews of Juan, the owner). Jaime, from PERRO Tour. We got off in Valparaiso after our South American cruise. Jaime met us at the entrance of the cruise terminal and gave us an impressive tour of Valparaiso using a car, funiculars, bus (the trolley was not able to go through). He always asked my husband whether he wants the car now. The car was always available for use if ever he felt tired and needed to rest or be driven. However, most of the fantastic sites can only be reached by walking so he opted to walk, always knowing a car is at hand with only a phone call. We got car service as soon as he asked for it,or whenever a scenery could be reached by a vehicle. We enjoyed our tour of Valparaiso and Vina del Mar tremendously, much better than expected. Great sites for history, scenic views and shopping. After our 5 hour tour (it was supposed to be 4 hrs only but I took a long time shopping for souvenirs), he and the driver even took us to the bus terminal in Vina Del Mar with our 4 luggages, which were stored in their car and they even helped us with our tickets to Santiago. Very cheap (< $10 only). Most of the tours and Internet companies charged a lot more: $150 car drive to Santiago w/o a tour from Valparaiso, others cost $150-$225 per person, tour with lunch from Valparaiso then proceeding to Santiago. Our great tour was less than $125 for both of us (we had lunch in Santiago) and the comfortable airconditioned bus ride from Valparaiso to Santiago was only 6000 pesos (<$10). What an amazing tour find and colorful city. Loved it! We're really glad you had an amazing tour and a wonderful time with Jaime and Perro Tour. You're right, most of the fantastic sites must be reached by walking, although the car allows us to move faster from one place to the next (which is important, when you're not able to walk a lot or want to visit Vina del Mar too). Over the last years, after hearing and reading the many compliments people have said on Perro Tour (and watching their happy and grateful faces too!), we've been committed to give the best walking tour experience in Valparaiso, as we've come to the conclusion that to get to really know the soul of Valpo, a tailored walking tour is the perfect option.

review_text: Torres del Paine took a long time to get to... the timetables practically require an overnight stay in Punta Arenas before heading north 3 hrs by bus to Puerto Natales, then you're still 2 hours drive away from the park. But it was totally worth the travel to see this amazing landscape. Many websites led me to believe that the only way to see this park is via a hike/trek over several days (not to say that a trek wouldn't have been amazing, we just didn't have the time). We found that there are many tours available that can be arranged through local operators for only a day trip, or two or three different day trips by car or minibus that don't require intense backpacking/hiking. The landscape is surreal with peaks of 9000 ft rising up from the valley. The lakes are an intense blue that photos can't capture. It was an experience I will always remember.

review_text: Amazing views of both the city and the mountains. It is worth a visit even after having visited Cerro San Cristobal. I recommend visiting aforementioned hill during day time and Sky Costanera at sunset. Photographers appreciate knowing that there was no problem taking a tripod up the tower and using it after the dark. There are several employees on the viewing platform, but nobody said anything to me about my tripod. Just keep everything in order and don't block other people's view and you will be fine. Photographers should also know that both the 61st floor and the open air 62nd floor have glass windows that produce lots of reflections. For unobstructed photos try having camera close to the corners (even behind the pillars) for more clear view. 61st floor is seemed slightly better in terms of reflections after it gets completely dark, so try both for better results. review_text: We decided to hike Volcán Villarica whilst in Pucon. With a multitude of companies offering the tour it’s tough to know where to start but in general you’re looking at 90-100,000 CLP. We decided to go with GoPucon because they said if we book there and then with cash we could have it for 80,000, which was cheaper than the other agencies we looked at. The agency took us via car at 6:30am from their office in town, to the base of the chair lift. You can do the first part of the hike by chair lift - a little pricey at 10,000 CLP but well worth it as it saves 1.5 hours roughly - the hike from the top of the chair lift is still a further 4 hours. GoPucon provide you with all the gear you need (trousers, jacket, gloves, hard hat, ice axe, gas mask and sledge). The pace of the hike was good - not too fast and not too slow, with multiple breaks for food and water on the way up. In all it took 4 hours to ascend. On the way down you toboggan part of the way down, which is really fun. The guides were friendly and helpful throughout. At the end of the day you’re dropped back at the office where there was snacks and beer waiting! Be prepared for a tough hike, but it’s entirely worth it at the top. I’m by no means an experienced trekker or walker and have average fitness and still managed it with no major issues. A big thumbs up from me!

review_text: I did the 4x day tour from San Pedro de Atacama on the 2nd of November. I'd read a lot of reviews about the salt flat tours and was concerned as most reviews seemed to say it was hit or miss but this one was an absolute bullseye Our guide Mijael (Magic Mike) was a legend! Great driver who was very safe and he knew absolutely loads about the different things we saw. Also had an aux cable so we could put our own music whilst driving through the incredible landscape which was a huge bonus for me. The tour itself was great. You spend a lot of time in the car but not necessarily a bad thing when you cover is much ground! You see some absolutely breathtaking scenery, and I fell in love with climbing the rocks that scattered the area. The best thing to do is go exploring a bit. I can't recommend enough when you stop somewhere don't just follow the tourists to the main spot, go for a wonder around as there are some magical spots First night accommodation is pretty basic, but the food is good and the people there are really friendly, there's a little shop around 10 minutes away you can buy a beer or some wine to have with dinner. Hot showers cost money but didn't bother me as I knew the next day they were free Second night accommodation is great! I am a solo travellor and I had my own room with private bathroom and hot water (heaven), great dinner and awesome.place to stargaze aswell The salt flats themselves are pretty damn special, watching the sunrise over the salt flats is something I won't forget. The famous perspective photo's were hilarious to be apart of and we had hours of fun messing around with different ideas. Although Mr Magic Mike definitely had the most ideas and was fantastic getting the photos done for us. Man of many talents Indeed! The last day is tough, it's literally a sprint back to Atacama as the tour really finishes on day 3 at the salt flats, and day 4 is just a transfer back. We lost magic Mike for the last day as we changed vehicle and the new driver was great but was also absolutely flying down the roads! Good fun but at times feels slightly unsafe. That's the only small negative I can think of this trip (really nitpicking) All in all fantastic experience, amazing guide, great company and would recommend every day

review_text: It is at the very end of the world (40 hours of travel for us that included 3 flights and a five hour drive on either end) but one of the most incredible adventures we have ever had. We hiked most of the classic "W" route tackling in three days 30k: day one Refugio Paine Grande to Valle Frances Mirador trailhead accessed by ferry over lago pehoe), day two Hotel Las Torres to Base de Las Torres and day three Refugio Grey to Refugio Paine Grande(accessed by the Lago Grey ferry which is an adventure in an of itself). We stayed two nights at Hotel Las Torres (highly recommended) and Hosteria Pehoe (reservedly recommended -- best view in the world offsets terrible service). We traveled in a small group with Southern Yosemite Mountain Guides out of California and they did a tremendous job of coordinating logistics which is no small thing in this enormous National Park. Frankly, we are too old and comfort seeking to stay in the refugios or campgrounds on the W route itself as thousands upon thousand of young hikers from all over the world are happy to do but we still love to hike! This is a gorgeous place with incredible vistas that no camera can completely do justice to. One thing to remember, Patagonia has the most dramatic weather including howling winds and rain with low clouds so you may want to build in an extra day or two into your itnerary to maximize your experience. We moved our hiking days around at the last minute so that our hike up to Las Torres would be on a sunny day and are really glad we did as it would be a shame to miss their grandeur if hidden in clouds.

review_text: We booked both the morning and afternoon tours to see and learn as much about the city in the short space of time we were there. Our guides were very knowledgeable and spoke excellent English. In the morning we visited some key sights and notable landmarks, and spent time in the vegetable market which was huge and really interesting, and we also here stopped for Chilean fruit drinks and street food (all included). We also visited the fish market which is in a very impressive building. The afternoon was mainly parks and politics and our guide spoke very eloquently to present a balanced description of the years under the Dictatorship. Our guide was Venezuelan, talked impressively about the history of Chile in impeccable English! A rather nice ice cream was also included! The total distance is about 15km, but it’s all flat and taken at a very leisurely pace. Helmets and sun cream are provided. The bikes have a basket so you can carry your bags and cameras etc. Almost the whole trip is on bike lanes which are clearly defined. There is a guide at the front and another at the rear, and for larger groups there is an extra guide to help with junctions etc. There was a short on-road section but the rear guide rode out to the side of us in the traffic so any cars had to clear him first. I really recommend this as a great day out to see the city up close. Review of: Santiago Bicycle Tour via Small Group: Parks, Markets and More Hi, Thanks so much for the detailed, positive review! It’s fantastic to hear that you had such a good time and found the material so interesting. As I’m sure you learned, Chilean politics is incredibly divisive, so it’s always very valuable when someone gives you a balanced, intelligent analysis of the dictatorship. Also, Santiago is the most bike friendly city in South America, and I think the sheer number of bike lanes that you all rode on proves it! At the same time, we also take safety very seriously, and it’s great that you felt so safe and confident on the ride. Thank you so much for your feedback, and if you’re ever back in Santiago, make sure to drop by the office! Safe travels, Peter

review_text: For months Andres worked with one of our group to plan and re-plan the details for our visit to Chile. All this was done via email; he was very timely in responding to emails and his English, both written and spoken, is excellent. From the moment he picked us at the airport in Puerto Montt midday on Saturday until he delivered us back to the airport a week plus later on Monday morning we enjoyed our trip. We spent two days exploring Chiloe Island and the wooden churches plus a boat trip to see penguins. We then stayed in a hotel in Puerto Varas for 5 nights during which Andres had arranged various activities of interest to us. One day he took 4 of us on a nearly 12 mile hike close to one of the snow covered volcanoes and ending near a gorgeous lake. This was NOT a hike you could tackle on your own because there were not clearly marked paths but he knows the area inside out. It was great being out where we encountered very few other humans but lots of interesting views. On another day a shorter hike in very different, more jungle like terrain. His knowledge of birds, animals and insects is amazing. He has contacts everywhere and when 2 of the group expressed interest in sea-kayaking he was immediately able to arrange that for one of the upcoming days. He also was a great source of restaurant recommendations within Puerto Varas and we were happy to share with him our own discoveries. Andres and his team seem capable of handling any size group and simple or complicated logistics. I have already recommended them to others considering a visit to Chile.

review_text: We saw a puma!!!!!!! OMG!!!!!! It is a beautiful park, the mountains, lakes, landscapes are stunning as is the wildlife. We saw foxs, wild horses, hares, guanacos, condors and a puma just hanging about and later sleeping with her cubs on rocks. Wow. It's not cheap visiting the park. The entrance fee for 3 days is fine and seems reasonable (they might even add extra days for you if you ask). It's not cheap because the nearest town in 2 hour car drive away. But food, camping, lodging and any ferry rides in the park are stupid, silly prices. We are not millionaires nor were we up for camping on O or W trek carrying our own stuff so we chose the cheapest alternative and I'm glad we did. After seeing how the O and W trek is organised the flexibility we had was easy better than the hikers on the treks, we also saw wildlife they didn't. We hired a car from Punta Arenas (cheaper than hiring in Puerto Natalies but we did have to take it back to PA) and stayed at a brilliant hostal in Puerto Natales, isla yu hostal. The hostal was a little out of town but because we had a car that didn't matter to us, what we did have was a shared kitchen, comfy beds, a warm place and good breakfasts. We drove to the park each day, yes it was 2 hours there and 2 hours back, yes the roads are a little sketchy but the views and wildlife you see make it worthwhile, we saw pumas early one morning. Downside is we got up early every day and got home late but we'd cooked our dinner in advance which helped. The other upside off doing it like this was we could chose what day to do which hikes, so we did the Torres del Paine hike on a perfect day, blue skies, hot sun, no wind. If you're on the O or W trek you have to go there on the date you are at the refugio close to it, it might be cloudy that day. I think the O and W trek makes for a very inflexible way of exploring the park and there are always lots of people around. We also got to see every mirador in the park and did fantastic hikes, glaciars, amazing viewpoints and most of the W trek anyway. We did hikes where we hardly saw any other people and then others where there were lots, basically any time we were on the W trek paths and of course at Torres del Paine, but that's to be expected.

review_text: I did the Bicicleta Verde bike and wine tour at Cousino Macul, which is outside of Santiago. The price was equivalent to $40 USD (cheaper to pay in Chilean pesos than online in USD), which is very expensive for what the tour is (in my opinion). For $40USD you get to ride on a bicycle for about 1 hour with minimal riding and you try one wine. The guide spoke English well and I learned a lot. Then you take a tour of the winery with one of the Cousino Macul employees who has a very thick accent, so I barely understood anything he said. Then you try 3 wines at the winery (very small amounts). The overall tour was about 2-3 hours (not including transportation, which you do on your own to and from the winery), minimal time on bicycles, a short winery tour (one of which is difficult to understand) and a free wine glass. The wine is delicious, don't get me wrong, but you don't get to try much of it. If you are not on a budget and have lots of money and time- then do this tour. If you are on a budget with only a day or two in Santiago, then I think that what you get for $40USD is not a lot, especially compared to the wine tasting amounts and tour costs in Mendoza... I would have preferred to do an Andes day hike rather than this tour with the little time I had in Santiago. Thanks Rachael for your feedback. review_text: Some kilometers out from the centre of town, this is what we might also call a folk or heritage museum that shows life back in the earlier days. There are a number of outdoor displays of mining and farming equipment such as old carts, drays, steam shovels and steam engines and we were a bit concerned about how these will survive over time being out in the elements. Under cover were old cars and buggies. Buildings to walk through included a dentistry, watchmakers, pharmacy, bakery and some residences. We were struck by how similar all these things are to the typical Australian pioneering ways. Guess our shared European heritage accounts for lots of commonalities.

review_text: This was the most amazing experience we spent together as a family, watching the skies darken on a crystal clear evening with very little moon light to spoil the dark skies. The gardens offer a brilliant haven to view the skies, set out with plenty of benches and beds with blankets so the visitor can sit or lay back, wrap up and enjoy every moment. After having a long exposure phot taken to make sure you have a lasting memory of the stars in the sky, for the last 15-20 minutes we were offered a very relaxing and calming sound experience of gentle gongs, with a mesmerising effect.

review_text: We arranged a tour with Cristian by email following the glowing reviews on Trip Advisor. My husband and I were travelling with two friends and arrived in Valparaiso at the cruise terminal where we were due to meet him and although we had arrived a little early there was Cristian bouncing with life and making us feel so welcome right from the start. We had booked two days with him, starting with a tour of the city of Valparaiso and its sister city of Vina Del Mar. Our driver was superb and we had a great day travelling around these two diverse cities and later they dropped us off at our hotel carrying our suitcases in. We had been able to leave these with our driver all day completely secure which was an added bonus. The next morning we were picked up by Cristian and driven to Isla Negra and had a great tour of the iconic home of Pablo Neruda, Chilean poet and diplomat. It was his favourite house and where he and his third wife, Matilde spent the majority of their time in Chile. Neruda, a lover of the sea and all things maritime, built the home to resemble a ship with low ceilings, creaking wood floors, and narrow passageways. A passionate collector, every room has a different collection of bottles, ship figureheads, maps, ships in bottles as well as an awesome array of shells, the likes of which we had never seen before. Neruda and his wife are buried there overlooking the ocean in such an idyllic spot. We moved on and had two awesome wine tours in the Casablanca Valley, one at a large winery and the other a smaller family concern, both were rewarding and we learned a lot about the wine process as well as sampling some excellent wines and picnicking in the most beautiful spot overlooking the fields of vines. We then travelled on to Santiago where Cristian safely delivered us to our hotel ready for our flight back to the UK the next day. The cost of our two days with him was not much more than what it would have cost us just for a city transfer so worth every penny. The four of us would highly recommend Cristian, his enthusiasm and energy and knowledge not only of the area but of anything one would wish to know about Chile was superb. We wish him well for the future and thank him for making our two days with him so magical as well as sending us some brilliant photographs he had taken as a reminder of our days with him in his beloved Chile.

review_text: We´ve skied a lot of places, and skiing in South America was on my bucket list. This met my expectations, but just know what you´re in for and you won´t be disappointed. The mountain is a lot like a Killington, VT above tree-line. Nice varied terrain for a variety of skiers, and with a ton of snow, experts can keep themselves busy. If you´re in for the week-long package, sign up for the three mountain pass (ski Valle Nevado, El Colorado and La Parva - all connected easily) and get happy with surface lifts. If your standard of skiing is the Rockies, the snow, terrain, lifts, etc will disappoint you. On the flip side, there are NO lift lines and early morning you have the mountain to yourself as our South American cousins wake up really late. Three hotels at Valle Nevado are well-appointed, but could use some maintenance. (there was a notable fire at Puerta del Sol that they hadn´t bothered trying to repair - charred exterior was front and center). Sheets are clean, bathrooms well maintained and the views from Puerta del Sol make this mid-priced hotel a nice option. Pool was clean and heated - and a nice break from skiing. Evening events and music were varied and fun for singles as well as families to participate in. Rooms were also quiet - we slept well and definitely needed the in-room humidifier that was offered. Don´t bother with the expensive restaurants on mountain. Stick to the price-included buffet dinner and breakfast. The buffets were well stocked, meat grilled custom, and the desserts give you a flavor of a few South American tastes (peruvian and brazilian favorites included). La Fourchette is overpriced and disappointing (took an hour to get our meal after ordering and it was oversalted) Don´t miss the crepe stand at mid-mountain. Salmon crepe was fresh and tasty, Dulce de Leche caramelly perfecto! Food in mid-mountain lodge is greasy, and the staff are cranky. This is a great place to bring kids. The staff in hotels and lifties were friendly and make a real effort to get to know your kids. Ski schools appear to be insanely crowded during the weekends with locals, sign up for mid-week lessons for your kiddos. Lastly, we enjoyed the medical services as well thanks to our daredevil 7-year-old. Don´t get injured here. The clinic is small, understaffed and dirty. If you have more than a sprain, you will be schlepped to Santiago, and then all bets are off. The medical staff are very friendly, and made every effort to communicate with us in english. One last thing - put EVERYTHING you buy on the room charge. Otherwise, you will be charged VAT which is 19% on top of the price of the item. Learn some spanish - you´ll be glad you did, and the staff will be happy you made the effort. Rude American and Brazilian tourists assumed the staff would be trilingual - unfair to the staff and frankly ridiculous. The language here is spanish, learn a few words and figure it out. Wifi is limited to the downstairs lobby and is very weak. They have internet kiosks to handle the most basic internet needs. But hey, you should be out skiing and taking pictures. The mountain itself has amazing, awe-inspiring views. There´s not a tree in sight, and the Andes are dark, spiky and beautiful with glaciers off in the distance. If South America is on your bucket list - go for Chile and leave overcrowded Argentina to the partiers.

review_text: Miguel Hott is a wonderful guide and we thoroughly enjoyed our day with him. After a few emails before and during our South America/Antarctica Cruise last month (February 2020), Miguel met us on time at the Puerto Montt cruise terminal for the start of our 6 hour tour of Frutillar, Llanquihue, and Puerto Varas. Miguel is fluent in English and we learned so much about Chile, the region, agriculture, daily life, recent changes in the area, and he was willing to answer every question and discuss any topic during our drive. He is very experienced and it is clear he loves to meet people from all over the world and be able to share his beautiful country with others. We were very fortunate to visit on a day with perfect weather—we had a number of stops during the day and the view of the Osorno Volcano and Calbuco Volcano across Lago Llanquihue became increasingly more beautiful and impressive as the day progressed. Our day with Miguel was a nice balance of time together and also time for us to explore (including the German Colonial Museum in Frutillar), shop, take photos, eat on our own. We highly recommend Miguel and would contact him again if we plan another trip to Chile, as he does other tours in the region.

Miguel is fluent in English and we learned so much about Chile, the region, agriculture, daily life, recent changes in the area, and he was willing to answer every question and discuss any topic during our drive. He is very experienced and it is clear he loves to meet people from all over the world and be able to share his beautiful country with others. We were very fortunate to visit on a day with perfect weather—we had a number of stops during the day and the view of the Osorno Volcano and Calbuco Volcano across Lago Llanquihue became increasingly more beautiful and impressive as the day progressed. Our day with Miguel was a nice balance of time together and also time for us to explore (including the German Colonial Museum in Frutillar), shop, take photos, eat on our own. We highly recommend Miguel and would contact him again if we plan another trip to Chile, as he does other tours in the region.

review_text: I did not take an organized tour but just rented a mountain bike to ride up San Cristobal hill. It was an excellent ride with spectacular views. The road up is a gentle hill for most of the way up. Almost no traffic other than bicycles. Then riding down the back side I got to see all of the things I didn't quite walk to when I rode the funicular up. After riding most of the roads you can exit near the central business district after a quick stop at the Japanese garden. Then you can ride back into town in a few minutes all on bike paths through a park. Hardly had to ride in traffic at all. Once downtown I still had an hour left on my 4 hour rental so I took the blue bike path to Quinta Normal Park (near the museum) and was able to ride around the whole park (again I only walked part of it before so this was a great bonus. There is a crazy looking church near the back that is work a look or a digital picture. Got back to the bike rental place in plenty of time and plenty hungry. Only downside is that I did this on my last day after I checked out of the hotel so I feel sorry for the person I sit next to on the overnight flight to the States. I'll try to clean up a bit before boarding the flight. This is a great ride for anyone that like to do recreational rides. Oh yea and the company (as always) was great-- they did what the promised at a reasonable price ($19,000 CL for 4 hours).

review_text: Fantastic. Highlight of my visit to Atacama and something I have wanted to do for years. We were lucky as some similar tours were cancelled because the sky was cloudy but the sky cleared just in time and ours went ahead. Renee the guide was a wonderful tutor and guide and imparted just the right amount of knowledge about what we were seeing - old stars, new stars, distant galaxies, Venus, Jupiter and its moons as clear as anything, Saturn and its rings. Mulled wine and small snacks on arrival, then viewing with the naked eye while Renee used a laser to point out what we were seeing, then four large telescopes that Renee helped ensure were focussed and pointed. Awe inspiring is the right way to describe what we saw. We get a photo of us against the starry sky as a momento. One small improvement would be to get acknowledgment of the booking and meeting place which we had to proactively confirm. This was the second time we used this company - the first was in December of 2016, when we went to Chile (Puerto Varas and Chiloe Island). I was very satisfied both times, since Jaime understood exactly what we wanted, and made sure that we got it (my younger son is disabled, so we have special needs). Everything went very smoothly, and the guides were knowledgeable and very helpful. They also pointed us to some excellent restaurants in Salvador and Rio, which added significantly to our overall experience. I should also mention that one of the tours was quite challenging (a day trip from Rio to Paraty, which involved more than 8 hours of driving in total). The driver made sure, however, that we made stops whenever needed, and navigated masterfully through traffic (which was heavy at times). Overall, I would recommend this company to anyone who is interested in customized private tours in South America. They are based in Chile, but Jaime has contacts in other countries as well, which provide the same level of service (in Brazil, he made all the arrangements through Be a Local Tours). He responds very quickly to e-mails, and provides very useful advice about what is feasible and what is not. He is definitely my go-to guy for South America. Thanks Alex, we have a great team for all the request..

review_text: We had a nice, relaxing walk of about 4 km from our Hostal in the centre of SP. We took off about 9am so it was a nice temperature & we just made sure we had water. The walk up the hill wasn't too hard, they have done it really well so that the paths aren't too steep but meander back & forward gradually getting you up higher. There are several rest stops that are sheltered so you can have a rest & admire the stunning views. We didn't get all the way up to the top, which I regret, but it was a bit much. Going back to town was a bit more challenging as the temperature had shot up a bit. Fortunately there was a food & drink caravan along the way so we could rest & refresh there for a while. We were just thinking what a long way back it was going to be when a local stopped & gave us a ride back to town. Would really recommend this one as something you can easily do on your own.

review_text: I was on my way to Santiago by bus, when, early in the morning, I decided to stop in Chanyaral and spend the day hiking in the national park. To my surprise, there was no public transportation, but luckily I found a taxi! For around 25 euros, a very friendly driver of an old vehicle (wish I remembered his name!) gave me a ride to Pan de Azucar. Fruits, water and sun lotion were my provisions for the day. I took the small route to the first view point from the park information office. Around 2 hours hike. The exciting views of Atacama were getting monotonous after a while... Almost no fauna in summer.. But then I reached the Mirador! Also, I found 4 more travelers admiring the contrast of the ocean and the desert. On the way back we took the summit path: a very good decision! A quick dive seemed to me a natural thing to do upon arrival to the beach.. It was my first an my last full contact with the South Pacific. Food was decent at the so-called fisherman restaurants. Well, don't expect too much. The most remarkable was the closing of the day. Breathtaking sunset on the sandy beach close to the camping.. Definitely worth it!!!

review_text: The underground (METRO) in Santiago is an essential part of getting around and will get you most places you want to go and many more as well. It has 4 major lines and you can (with some concentration) switch between one line and another. To use the system, you must initially purchase a “BIP” card from a station (cost about 1300 pesos) and then you put the required amount of money on the card to be deducted. A Journey costs 680 pesos whether it is for one station or for twenty stations. Similarly, you can change lines and not pay again as long as you keep your wits about you and do not walk out of the gates. Because it is a single charge irrespective of length of ride, there is no need to swipe the card when leaving the station – just walk through a sprung low door. One of the good things about the system is that multiple people can use the same card one after the other – saving the initial card purchase cost. The holder touches on for each person that goes through the turnstile and then finally for themselves. Just remember to load enough money onto the card for the total number of journeys you might expect to make. We spend 4000 pesos to buy the card and put initial credit on it and later put more credit on as we used the Metro more than we expected. The Metro has very frequent trains – every 3 to 5 minutes but they can be very full at peak times and have only limited seats, so you may be standing. They run on rubber tyres but are still quite noisy. A hazard for the unprepared are buskers who often come on with a battery powered amplifier and start singing. Some can be good, but most are just noise and the worst will blast you with a wall of noise in a crowded train where the you cannot move away. If you see someone with a set of speakers on wheels waiting to board the train, move to the entrance for another carriage so they will not spoil your trip. There are also buses that connect at most stations to other areas, but if you are going a short distance taxis in Santiago are cheap – but as always- make sure that they have and use a meter !! The Metro in Santiago is a safe and efficient and relatively inexpensive was to get to key points around and within the city.

review_text: Thomas was a pleasure to work with and did a great job planning our 2 days after a Viking cruise with another couple. He met us at the cruise terminal with a van with room for plenty of luggage and a driver. We spent 2 hours on a walking tour of Valapraiso seeing many different parts of the city and many beautiful murals. After the tour we drove to the Casablanca Valley to the Kingston Family Vineyards where we had the best lunch and wine tastings of our life. The lunch was 5 course meal with wine pairings. review_text: We wanted to fetbour of the city and see some more rural territory so this seemed a good idea. We lived the whole day. Prior to getting there we stopped at a roadside restaurant which had a somewhat rundown backyard with 1 old horse and about 5 lamas, one of shom had a broken leg so it walked on 3 but it was sad to see it. The yard Aldo had a half full swimming pool of green brackish water, also a put off for tourists. But the guide had purchased wine at the vineyard we stopped at earlier and this restaurant made fantastic empanadas so we had a rough and ready picnic....not my first choice, I'd rather have eaten in the restaurant and not sat looking at rather sad disabled animals. Alpacas and Vicinas up in Peru the 3 weeks previously but most of the folks in this small group tour hadn't been up close to any of them so for them it was a novelty. For the $$ spent, there is definitely room for improvement - I guess the good things make up for the not so good.

review_text: Our tour was booked for an 8:00 pickup. The instructions were for us to wait inside the cruise port gate. They said do not go out to the street. At 8:15 another guide told us that Pedro was waiting for us on the street outside the gate. Pedro said that did not expect us until 8:30. Fifteen minutes after our van finally left the port, we again went past the port. Pedro said the driver had gone the wrong way. After our 1st walk we waited 15 minutes for our van although there was no traffic being Sunday morning. Other than those issues the tour went well and Valparaíso is beautiful. Thank you for your review, Gregory! Be excellent, average, or poor, your comments about your experience with Perro Tour are extremely important to us. We would have been happy if your experience had been fantastic instead of decent and, clearly, understand that the unexpected issues regarding the short delay at the beginning of the tour and while waiting for the driver, to meet you and Pedro in Valparaiso, were not acceptable at all, and that away affected your overall experience. Just to clarify the issues you addressed: -It was my personal mistake to tell Pedro, your guide, to meet you at 8:30. Anyway, when Pedro called me at 8:04 (while I was with you), he had already arrived one or two minutes before (this timing is according to my phone, which is perfectly set to the official time in Chile). Then, as you probably noticed, vans cannot park at the port in San Antonio (only buses and vans doing official tours from the cruise company can). Due to this fact, once any guide from any tour company meets its group, he/she has to call the driver to meet them at the entrance of the port. The whole journey from where drivers can park to the entrance of the port is about 2 km (10 minutes if they don't get a red light), since downtown San Antonio is so narrow, and streets around the port are just 1 lane streets. -We're sorry that the driver had gone the wrong way, which means that you lost some minutes (about 5-10 minutes) from the tour. -We understand your discomfort when you had to wait 15 minutes (as you quoted) for the driver, after your first walk. For what I was informed by Pedro, the driver had to change one of the wheel tyres. Sadly, this kind of issues can arise sometimes, though it is actually the first time it has happened to us after six years and hundreds of tours, since we started. I hope that if you ever come back to Valparaiso, we can have the chance to change your experience for the better. Best regards, Juan Victor
